Article Title: Microsoft net income rises 32% to $36.6 billion days after buyout offer to 60,000 staff
Article Text:
Microsoft posts $36.6 billion profit as 60,000 staff offered voluntary exits

Microsoft Cloud revenue rises 30%, Azure grows 48%

Microsoft projects December-quarter revenue of up to $97.1 billion

Capital expenditure expected to exceed $50 billion in December quarter

Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees

Microsoft reported a 32 per cent year-on-year rise in net income to $36.6 billion in the July-September quarter, days after announcing a voluntary buyout offer for around 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its global workforce.India is among the four countries where the offer applies, alongside the US, Canada and the UK.The technology major began fiscal year 2027 with higher revenue and earnings, supported by strong growth in its cloud business. Revenue for the first quarter ended September 30, 2026, rose 19 per cent to $92.3 billion from $77.7 billion in the corresponding quarter last year. Operating income increased 21 per cent to $45.9 billion.Microsoft's cloud business remained a key contributor to its results, with Microsoft Cloud revenue reaching $63.9 billion, up 30 per cent year-on-year and 31 per cent in constant currency. Azure revenue grew 48 per cent during the quarter.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella highlighted the performance in a post on X. “Just wrapped our earnings call. It was a fast start to our fiscal year. Microsoft Cloud revenue surpassed $63B, with growth accelerating to 30% YoY,” he said.Revenue from Microsoft's Agents and Infra segment rose 25 per cent to $76.8 billion. The company's commercial remaining performance obligation, which represents contracted revenue yet to be recognised, increased 73 per cent to $677 billion.“We delivered a strong start to the fiscal year with Microsoft Cloud revenue of $63.9 billion, with growth accelerating to 30% (up 31% in constant currency) year-over-year,” said Amy Hood, Microsoft's executive vice president and chief financial officer. She added that the company exceeded expectations across revenue, operating income and earnings per share.Diluted earnings per share increased 32 per cent to $4.92 on a reported basis. Excluding the impact of investments in OpenAI, adjusted net income rose 18 per cent to $36.4 billion, while adjusted earnings per share increased 18 per cent to $4.89.Microsoft expects revenue of $96 billion to $97.1 billion in the December quarter, representing growth of 18-19 per cent. Azure revenue growth is projected at 49-50 per cent in constant currency.Hood said customer demand continues to exceed available supply, while improvements in the efficiency of the company's computing infrastructure are helping it serve more demand.Microsoft's capital expenditure stood at $45.2 billion in the September quarter. Hood expects spending to exceed $50 billion in the December quarter, with capital expenditure for calendar year 2026 projected at approximately $170 billion. The estimate partly reflects capacity deliveries delayed from earlier periods.However, not all business segments recorded growth. Revenue from Microsoft's Devices and Consumer segment declined 3 per cent to $15.5 billion. Windows OEM and devices revenue fell 22 per cent, while Xbox content and services revenue declined 2 per cent. Search and advertising revenue, excluding traffic acquisition costs, grew 12 per cent.The company's financial performance comes as it offers voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its global workforce. Chief people officer Amy Coleman announced the Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) in a memo to staff on Monday, presenting it as an option for employees already considering a future outside Microsoft to leave with financial support and career planning assistance.The terms mirror Microsoft's standard severance arrangements. Eligible employees in the US, Canada, the UK and India at level 70 and below have until the first week of December to decide whether to accept the offer. The level band extends up to general managers and some vice presidents. Employees who accept will leave the company at the end of the year.Unlike the retirement buyout Microsoft offered earlier this year, the VEO has no age or tenure requirement, and performance does not determine eligibility.However, the offer is not available to every employee at level 70 or below. Microsoft has left the decision on participation to individual business leaders. Coleman's memo said participation would depend on each unit's priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.
Article Summary: Microsoft posts $36.6 billion profit as 60,000 staff offered voluntary exits. Cloud revenue rises 30%, Azure grows 48% in July-September quarter. Microsoft projects December-quarter revenue of up to $97.1 billion.Capital expenditure expected to exceed $50 billion in December quarter.

Article Title: Google parent Alphabet loses $500 billion in market value as AI spending spooks investors
Article Text:
The $500 billion wipeout marked the second-largest single-day loss in market value recorded by a company, after chipmaker Nvidia lost nearly $600 billion in early 2025

AI spending raises questions about returns

Why investors are becoming cautious about AI

Shares of Google parent Alphabet plunged more than 12% on Thursday, wiping out around $500 billion in market value in one of the biggest single-day losses in stock market history. The sell-off reflected growing investor concerns over the company's escalating artificial intelligence spending, slowing growth in its search advertising business and uncertainty over how quickly its investments will generate returns.The decline marked Alphabet's worst single-day fall on record, exceeding its losses during the Covid-19 pandemic and the 2008 financial crisis, according to CNN. The market value erosion was the second-largest single-day loss recorded by a company, after chipmaker Nvidia lost nearly $600 billion in early 2025.The sharp fall followed Alphabet's quarterly earnings report, released on Wednesday, which showed sales below analysts' expectations. Investors were particularly concerned about the outlook for Google's search advertising business, which has long been a major source of revenue and profit.The company is facing growing competition from artificial intelligence-powered chatbots that allow users to seek information without relying on traditional search results. Investors fear this shift could weaken Google's advertising business if consumers increasingly turn to AI tools, including those developed by competitors, to find answers online.The concern is that the transition could happen faster than Google can adapt its business model. Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, told CNN that the displacement of traditional search could happen “faster than Google can react to it and pivot their business.”Alongside concerns about its core search business, Alphabet's rapidly rising expenditure on AI infrastructure has intensified scrutiny of its financial performance.The company reported $51.4 billion in capital expenditure in the third quarter alone, compared with $91.4 billion for the whole of 2025. The spending includes investments in data centres and computing infrastructure needed to develop and operate AI services.While technology companies are pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into infrastructure to compete in the AI race, investors are increasingly questioning whether the spending will translate into sustainable profits.A key concern for Alphabet is its free cash flow, which measures the cash remaining after operating expenses and capital investments. The company recorded negative free cash flow for a second consecutive quarter, according to CNN. Before this year, Google had not reported a negative figure for any quarter since going public in 2004.Negative free cash flow does not necessarily indicate that a company is unprofitable. However, it means less cash is available after investment spending to fund shareholder returns, including dividends and share buybacks, or to support other business priorities.Alphabet's performance stood in contrast to Microsoft, which reported $18.6 billion in free cash flow for the third quarter despite continuing to invest heavily in AI infrastructure. Microsoft's shares ended Thursday's session largely unchanged, while Alphabet suffered a double-digit decline.“We are now getting to see who is spending rationally on AI and who is not,” Richard Reyle, chief investment officer at Questar Capital Partners, told CNN.The sell-off highlights a broader shift in how markets are evaluating the AI boom. Investors are no longer looking only at the scale of companies' investments or the growth potential of the technology. They are also assessing whether those investments can generate adequate returns, how much cash they consume and whether AI could undermine existing revenue streams.Alphabet is attempting to expand its AI capabilities while defending its dominant search business. Its investments could help it compete in a rapidly changing technology market, but the returns remain uncertain as the industry races to build data centres and secure computing capacity.Even the prospect of future demand from AI companies does not guarantee immediate profitability. Although AI firms are committing to large amounts of computing power, the financial benefits depend on whether demand continues to grow and whether the infrastructure can be monetised at a sufficient scale.Technology companies are also increasingly turning to debt and financial markets to fund their ambitions, raising questions about the sustainability of the industry's capital spending.“Everybody is trying to get through the door at the same time, and it gives people pause,” Ted Mortonson, a technology-focused investment strategist at Baird, told CNN.For Alphabet, the challenge is to demonstrate that its massive AI investments can produce profitable growth without weakening the cash-generating search business that has supported the company for years. Thursday's steep decline suggests investors are demanding clearer evidence of those returns rather than accepting spending growth as a sign of future success.
Article Summary: Shares of Google parent Alphabet plunged more than 12% on Thursday, wiping out around $500 billion in market value. The sell-off reflected growing investor concerns over the company's escalating artificial intelligence spending, slowing growth in its search advertising business and uncertainty over how quickly its investments will generate returns. The decline marked Alphabet's worst single- day fall on record.

Article Title: Amazon shares sink 7% as AI spending fuels cash-burn concerns, overshadow cloud growth
Article Text:
Amazon cloud business accelerates but shares drop on profit miss

Cash burn and outlook weigh on sentiment

Advertising business misses expectations

AI spending pressures spread across Big Tech

Amazon shares fell sharply in after-hours trading on Thursday (local time) as heavy artificial intelligence investments and a weaker-than-expected earnings performance overshadowed accelerating growth in its cloud computing business.The e-commerce and technology giant’s shares dropped as much as 7% after it reported third-quarter results that missed Wall Street expectations and issued a cautious revenue outlook for the crucial holiday shopping quarter. The stock had already fallen 4.3% during regular trading to close at $243.79.Amazon’s cloud computing unit, Amazon Web Services (AWS), delivered a standout performance, with revenue rising 39% year-on-year to $46 billion in the quarter ended September 30. This marked its fastest growth in nearly five years and accelerated from the 37% increase recorded in the previous quarter. Revenue also exceeded analysts’ expectations of $45.61 billion, according to LSEG data.However, investors remained concerned about the cost of expanding the business to capitalise on growing demand for artificial intelligence. Amazon has forecast capital expenditure of $220 billion for 2026, largely to build AI data centres and expand its technology infrastructure.Chief executive Andy Jassy told analysts that capital expenditure would be “meaningfully more” next year, without providing a specific figure. “Our strategy is working and I expect it will for the foreseeable future,” Jassy said, defending the company’s investment plans.He also said AWS could become a business generating more than $1 trillion in annual revenue within five to 10 years, adding that demand for the unit’s services remained strong.“Customers are gobbling it up,” Jassy said, referring to the rapid adoption of Amazon’s AI infrastructure.Amazon’s spending plans have raised questions about how quickly its AI investments will translate into stronger cash generation. The company reported a trailing 12-month cash burn of $42.4 billion in the September quarter, driven by heavy capital expenditure. Spending on capital projects during the quarter reached $77.26 billion, around $20 billion above estimates compiled by LSEG.“The free cash flow looks like the ugly part of the report,” said Dave Wagner, portfolio manager at Aptus Capital Advisors. “Operations generated plenty of cash but their capex just absolutely swallowed it.”Amazon reported net sales of $201.94 billion for the quarter, up 12% from $180.17 billion a year earlier. Net income declined to $20.69 billion, or $1.89 per share, from $21.19 billion, or $1.95 per share, in the year-ago period. Analysts had expected earnings of $1.97 per share on revenue of $202.2 billion, according to FactSet.The company forecast fourth-quarter net sales of between $240 billion and $247 billion, representing growth of 12% to 16% from a year earlier. The midpoint of the range, $243.5 billion, was slightly below analysts’ estimate of $244.51 billion, according to LSEG.The outlook covers the holiday shopping season, a crucial period for Amazon’s retail business, as consumers contend with elevated living costs and higher fuel prices.Amazon’s advertising division also disappointed investors. Revenue rose 12 per cent to $19.6 billion, falling short of analysts’ expectations for growth of 18%. It was the first time in seven quarters that the business missed estimates, according to Reuters.The slowdown contrasted with growth of 26% in the previous quarter and 22% in the year-ago period. Jassy attributed some of the weakness to the timing of the company’s Prime Day shopping event, which took place in the second quarter this year in most major markets, including the US.Amazon said the shift in Prime Day’s timing also affected its overall third-quarter sales growth. Excluding the calendar change, year-on-year revenue growth would have been approximately four percentage points higher, the company said.Amazon’s results come amid growing investor scrutiny of the enormous sums technology companies are committing to AI infrastructure and whether the spending will deliver adequate returns.Alphabet, the parent company of Google and YouTube, saw its shares plunge 12% on Thursday after investors reacted to its latest results and rising expenditure on property and equipment. Microsoft, meanwhile, lowered its capital expenditure outlook to $170 billion from $175 billion.The sell-off reflects concerns that the race to build data centres and deploy AI chips could strain cash flows even at some of the industry’s largest companies.Amazon is also facing scrutiny over the impact of its expanding data centre footprint on local communities. Earlier this month, the company said it would invest more than $1 billion over five years in communities where it operates data centres, including funding for education, job training, water conservation and energy-related initiatives.Despite the concerns, Amazon continues to expand its retail operations through faster deliveries, automation and AI-powered warehouse technology. Jassy has argued that these investments are strengthening the company’s competitive position, while the latest AWS results indicate that demand for its cloud infrastructure remains robust.
Article Summary: Amazon shares fell sharply in after-hours trading on Thursday (local time) as heavy artificial intelligence investments and a weaker-than-expected earnings performance overshadowed accelerating growth in its cloud computing business. The e-commerce and technology giant’s shares dropped as much as 7% after it reported third-quarter results that missed Wall Street expectations.

Article Title: 3 Wall Street firms agree to pay up to $100,000 a month to get Trump’s posts faster: How it works
Article Text:
3 trading firms agree to pay Trump’s Truth Social for faster access

How Truth API works

Who is paying for the service?

Why the paid feed has drawn criticism

Trump Media’s financial portfolio

US President Donald Trump’s paid social media service, Truth API, has found customers, with Bloomberg and two high-frequency trading firms paying for faster access to his posts. The service costs financial institutions up to $100,000 a month.Two sources with direct knowledge of the matter, cited by Reuters, said Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading, both of which specialise in algorithmic and automated trading strategies, have also signed up for the service.The deals give subscribers a timing advantage over people who monitor Trump’s posts on the app themselves.The arrangement has raised concerns about the sale of faster access to statements by a sitting president, particularly because his posts can influence financial markets.It also comes as Trump Media and Technology Group, the company behind Truth Social, faces legal challenges over the paid service and questions about the potential use of presidential communications for commercial gain.Trump Media and Technology Group announced the faster-access product in July, pitching it to trading firms and other financial institutions. The service is designed to deliver Trump’s posts more quickly than a person could obtain them by repeatedly checking Truth Social.Trump Media officials have put the timing advantage at 50 milliseconds. For financial firms using automated trading systems, that difference can matter when a presidential statement triggers a change in asset prices.High-frequency traders rely on software to scan news headlines, company announcements and government statements for information that could move markets. Their systems can read and analyse the information before executing trades in thousandths of a second.The potential consequences of Trump’s social media posts were evident in April, when oil futures fell after he announced a ceasefire in the Iran war on Truth Social.An application programming interface, or API, acts as a digital bridge that allows one computer system to communicate with another. In this case, the product gives subscribers faster access to the president’s posts, which they can use in their trading or financial information systems.According to a Reuters report, Bloomberg, Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading are among the organisations that have signed up for Truth API.In August, Trump Media told investors it had "signed more than 10 customer agreements”. Reuters was unable to independently confirm that figure.The company did not identify its customers but said they were primarily Wall Street trading firms paying between $60,000 and $100,000 a month. The latest deals indicate that the product has attracted both financial trading firms and a news and data provider.Reuters, which competes with Bloomberg in financial news, said in a statement: "We will assess the service, but have no current plans to subscribe."Trump Media defended the product in a statement, saying: “Truth Social offers an industry-standard API product for which there is significant demand across industries. We take customer confidentiality seriously. This reporting is based on misleading information being peddled by anonymous sources aimed at harming our company, customers and shareholders.”The company has not publicly named the subscribers in its August investor update, and the three firms named in the report declined to comment.The paid service has drawn criticism for giving subscribers faster access to a president’s statements, potentially offering financial firms an advantage when his posts move markets. The deals are likely the first time a business linked to a sitting president has sold access to his statements.In July, Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and Adam Schiff of California asked the US Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate whether the service violated securities laws. They called it a “shocking abuse” of office by a president seeking personal gain.A Trump Media and Technology Group spokesperson said, “Congressional Democrats continue to mischaracterize Truth API either out of ideological opposition to free markets or a failure to grasp the distinction between public and nonpublic information.”In August, Intercept Media and the non-profit Freedom of the Press Foundation sued Trump, seeking to stop the White House from posting official government announcements exclusively on Truth Social. The ongoing lawsuit describes the service as "profoundly corrupt" and alleges violations of the First and Fifth Amendments.The commercial arrangement has also drawn attention to the ownership of Trump Media. The president’s family trust owns 41% of the company, and Trump is the trust’s sole beneficiary.The Truth API deals come as Trump Media faces a steep decline in its stock market value.Shares of the company have fallen more than 50% so far this year. Its market value has also been volatile since it went public in March 2024.The company closed at a market value of about $8 billion on its debut in March 2024, but is now worth about $1.8 billion.Since 2024, Trump Media has lost about $1.76 billion, including non-cash charges.
Article Summary: Bloomberg, Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading are among the organisations that have signed up for Truth API. The service is designed to deliver Trump’s posts more quickly than a person could obtain them by repeatedly checking Truth Social. For financial firms using automated trading systems, that difference can matter when a presidential statement triggers a change in asset prices.

Article Title: Oil prices rise as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia stoke supply fears; Brent nears $116
Article Text:
Brent futures gained 86 cents, or 0.75%, to $115.74 a barrel

Peace overtures fail to ease tensions

Crude oil prices continued their upward march on Friday, with Brent crossing $115 a barrel as attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and mounting risks to shipping in the Gulf heightened fears of supply disruptions. The benchmarks were also heading for their fourth consecutive monthly rise, with US crude poised to settle above $100 for the first time since April.Brent futures gained 86 cents, or 0.75 per cent, to $115.74 a barrel by 0122 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 72 cents, or 0.71 per cent, to $102.72.Brent was on course for a nearly 14 per cent gain in October, while WTI was set to jump around 15 per cent. Both were heading for their sharpest monthly increases since July.The latest escalation came on Thursday, when Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group claimed attacks on key Saudi oil installations, including the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries and an Aramco facility in Abqaiq. A Saudi-led coalition separately reported intercepting a cruise missile launched towards the kingdom’s western region.The developments have heightened concerns over the security of energy infrastructure and shipping routes at a time when prospects for a diplomatic breakthrough remain uncertain.“Continued kinetic action around the Strait of Hormuz amidst doubts of a viable diplomatic pathway are keeping oil prices elevated in expectation of an escalation of the conflict in coming weeks,” said Saul Kavonic, head of energy research at MST Marquee.The Strait of Hormuz remains a major source of concern for energy markets, with any disruption to traffic through the waterway threatening to constrain global oil supplies.Efforts to reopen diplomatic channels between Washington and Tehran have yet to provide markets with reassurance.US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Vice President JD Vance had contacted Iran to help it obtain medical supplies. This followed US media reports that Vance had written to Iran’s top security official in a bid to restart peace negotiations.Iran has received the letter but has not responded, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported. Tehran is insisting that Washington accept its conditions, the agency said, quoting the Iranian position that “any position that contradicts this framework is unacceptable.”At sea, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards reported that three tankers had hit sea mines, exploded and caught fire while attempting to use an unauthorised route south of the Strait of Hormuz. The report added to the security concerns surrounding maritime traffic in the region.The heightened risks are also prompting changes to corporate travel plans. ExxonMobil and Chevron have cancelled plans for their executives to attend the United Arab Emirates’ biggest oil show next week, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.With crude prices already recording substantial monthly gains, traders are watching for signs that the conflict could further disrupt oil production or transportation. The trajectory of diplomatic efforts and the security of key energy routes are likely to remain central to market sentiment.
Article Summary: Brent futures gained 86 cents, or 0.75%, to $115.74 a barrel. US crude poised to settle above $100 for the first time since April. Attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and mounting risks to shipping in the Gulf have heightened fears of supply disruptions.

Article Title: GST collections rise 22.9% to Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October
Article Text:
Net revenue after refunds grew 25.6 per cent to Rs 2.03 lakh crore, with import-related collections recording a sharp 42.2 per cent increase.

NEW DELHI: The gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections rose 22.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October, supported by a sharp increase in revenue from imports and steady growth in domestic collections, provisional government data showed on Sunday.The October collection compares with Rs 1.88 lakh crore recorded in the same month last year. After adjusting for refunds, net GST revenue grew 25.6 per cent to Rs 2.03 lakh crore, against Rs 1.61 lakh crore a year ago.Revenue from imports was the bigger contributor to the increase, rising 42.2 per cent to Rs 72,246 crore from Rs 50,796 crore in October 2025. Collections from domestic transactions grew 15.8 per cent to Rs 1.59 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.37 lakh crore in the year-ago period.The government issued refunds worth Rs 27,934 crore during the month, 6.5 per cent higher than in October last year. Domestic refunds increased 9.8 per cent to Rs 14,007 crore, while refunds on imports rose 3.4 per cent to Rs 13,927 crore.After adjusting for refunds, net revenue from domestic transactions grew 16.4 per cent to Rs 1.45 lakh crore. Net collections from customs-related GST rose 56.2 per cent to Rs 58,319 crore.Among major states, Maharashtra recorded domestic GST collections of Rs 35,150 crore, up 13 per cent year-on-year. Karnataka's collections increased 18 per cent to Rs 15,922 crore, while Gujarat reported a 16 per cent rise to Rs 13,516 crore. Haryana recorded a 17 per cent increase to Rs 11,529 crore.Assam saw one of the sharpest increases, with collections rising 47 per cent to Rs 1,934 crore. Uttar Pradesh and Bihar both recorded 24 per cent growth."October’s gross GST collections of Rs 2.31 lakh crore, registering a robust 22.9% year-on-year growth, reinforce the continued buoyancy in GST revenues. Importantly, this strength is not limited to a single month, with cumulative gross collections during April–October reaching Rs 14.78 lakh crore, representing a healthy 13.2% year-on-year growth. This sustained revenue buoyancy, despite bold rate cuts mid last year, is providing the confidence and headroom for the GST Council to continue with the reform express," said Mahesh Jaising, partner & leader indirect tax, Deloitte India.While, Abhishek Jain, partner and national head indirect tax for Kpmg in India, said, “The GST collection figures with a growth of 22.9% for October 2026 is impressive and adds to the festive cheer. The cumulative gross GST collections for April–October 2026 have also grown by 13.2% reflecting sustained economic activity, improved tax compliance and the continued resilience of India's consumption and trade ecosystem. Overall, the October numbers provide a positive signal for revenue mobilisation and reinforce the growing maturity of India's GST framework.”Nitin Vijaivergia, partner, Price Waterhouse & Co LLP, also higlhighted the strong momentum saying, "October’s GST collections of Rs 2.31 lakh crore, the second-highest monthly collection on record, reflect strong revenue momentum. Domestic collections grew 15.8%, signalling healthy consumption and economic activity, while import revenues surged 42.2%, highlighting the increasing contribution of imports to overall GST revenues. This trend merits attention from a domestic manufacturing perspective. Encouragingly, net GST revenues grew even faster at 25.6%, with refunds rising only 6.5%. Cumulative April-October collections grew 13.2%, further indicating that the revenue buoyancy is broad-based and extends beyond a single month."For the first seven months of the current financial year, gross GST collections rose 13.2 per cent to Rs 14.77 lakh crore, compared with Rs 13.05 lakh crore during April-October last year. Net collections during the period increased 12.6 per cent to Rs 12.69 lakh crore.The October figures mark a strong year-on-year increase in tax collections, with both domestic activity and imports contributing to the growth.
Article Summary: Net revenue after refunds grew 25.6 per cent to Rs 2.03 lakh crore, with import- related collections recording a sharp 42.2 per cent increase. The government issued refunds worth Rs 27,934 crore during the month, 6.5 per cent higher than in October last year.

Article Title: India's record oil imports hit 5.6 million bpd as Middle East, Russia supplies rise: Report
Article Text:
India's crude oil imports hit a record 5.6 million barrels per day in October, but rising freight costs and competitive Gulf prices could make Russian supplies less attractive

How Russia became a key supplier

NEW DELHI: India's crude oil imports hit a record high of around 5.6 million barrels per day (bpd) in October, with refiners stepping up purchases from both the Middle East and Russia. While improved supplies through the Strait of Hormuz have boosted Gulf shipments, rising freight costs could make Russian crude less attractive in the coming months, according to energy intelligence firm Kpler.Middle Eastern supplies accounted for about 2.3 million bpd, while Russian shipments remained strong at nearly 2 million bpd, Kpler lead analyst Nikhil Dubey said, as quoted by PTI.The increase in Gulf supplies comes as more crude is moving through the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil trade. Higher ship-to-ship transfers helped boost flows through the strait during September and October.Gulf producers are also offering competitive delivered prices to regain market share in India. This could make their supplies more attractive to refiners in the coming months, particularly as the cost of transporting Russian crude rises.Dubey said Russian shipments could moderate in November and December as attacks in the Black Sea push up freight rates, reducing the price advantage of Russian oil once transportation costs are included."Russian flows, which have held strong at these levels, could soften in November-December as attacks in the Black Sea push freight rates higher, making Russian barrels less attractive on a landed cost basis," he said.However, a shift towards Middle Eastern supplies may depend on how the situation around Hormuz unfolds. Any renewed disruption to shipments through the strait could make Gulf crude harder to secure and prompt Indian refiners to return to Russian barrels, even at higher freight costs."The situation remains volatile, and any renewed disruption to Hormuz flows could see refiners turning back to Russian barrels, even at higher freight costs," Dubey said.The October 16 waiver under the Graham Act could also ease concerns among some Indian buyers about the risks associated with purchasing Russian oil, giving them greater flexibility in sourcing supplies, he added.India imports nearly 90 per cent of its crude oil requirements, making the availability, transportation costs and final landed price of different grades important factors in procurement decisions.India's dependence on Russian crude rose sharply after Moscow invaded Ukraine in February 2022. Western sanctions, the European Union's ban on seaborne Russian crude and a G7 price cap disrupted Russia's traditional oil trade, forcing it to look for alternative buyers.With European refiners turning away from Russian supplies, Moscow offered steep discounts to attract customers. Indian refiners emerged as major buyers, with Russian crude eventually accounting for as much as 40-50 per cent of India's oil basket at its peak.The price advantage was significant. Russian Urals crude traded at discounts of around $30 per barrel to Brent at times in late 2022 and early 2023, making it an attractive option for Indian refiners seeking to lower input costs.Those discounts have since narrowed. Yet Russian shipments have remained substantial, partly because disruptions to Middle Eastern supplies have made alternative sources important for India's energy security.
Article Summary: India's crude oil imports hit a record high of around 5.6 million barrels per day in October. Middle Eastern supplies accounted for about 2.3 million bpd, while Russian shipments remained strong. Rising freight costs and competitive Gulf prices could make Russian supplies less attractive in the coming months.

Article Title: Binance resumes Bitcoin withdrawals after $6.3bn hack, says 95% of assets replaced
Article Text:
The first phase covers 15 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether, XRP and Dogecoin.

FBI links $6.3 billion hack to North Korean hackers

Binance uses company funds to cover losses

Binance thanks US agencies for tracking stolen funds

Binance resumed withdrawals of Bitcoin, Ether and some stablecoins on Sunday after hackers stole $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from the exchange. The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange said it had replaced 95 per cent of the stolen assets using its own funds, while withdrawals of other cryptocurrencies would resume in phases.The first phase covers 15 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether, XRP and Dogecoin. Bitcoin withdrawals resumed shortly after 0600 GMT, followed by Ether, BNB and some stablecoins, including USDT and USDC.Binance said it had spent around $6 billion buying replacement tokens. The remaining 5 per cent of stolen assets comprises less liquid cryptocurrencies that could take longer to source in the required quantities.The FBI on Saturday attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a cyber unit sponsored by the North Korean state. The agency said it had observed members of the group converting stolen assets into Ether and expected further attempts to launder the funds.North Korea has repeatedly denied using state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue generation. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests for comment.US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis had also linked the attack to North Korea. They said most of the theft took place within around 20 minutes late on Thursday, bearing similarities to previous cyberattacks attributed to the country.However, US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that Washington was not yet certain whether North Korea was involved.Binance said it had been working with industry partners to freeze the stolen assets, with around $3 billion located by Friday. The exchange has repeatedly assured customers that it would absorb the financial losses rather than pass them on to users.The company has set aside around $6.34 billion to cover the damage. Funds used to buy replacement tokens came from its corporate treasury, part of its Futures Insurance Fund and its $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a reserve designed to protect customers during security breaches.Binance co-CEO Yi He said on Saturday that half of the SAFU funds would be used, with the company committing to replenish the reserve to around $1 billion.Binance thanked the FBI for its assistance in a post on X referring to the agency's statement on North Korea's alleged involvement. The exchange did not respond to a request for comment on the attribution.Founder Changpeng Zhao also credited US law enforcement agencies with helping track and freeze the stolen assets."A tweet can't fully express our gratitude. Many crypto bros may not realize, a lot of the 'why bitcoin didn't drop more?' credit goes to them," Zhao wrote.Zhao was convicted in the US of failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering programme at Binance. US President Donald Trump pardoned him last year.The attack comes amid a wider rise in cryptocurrency thefts. Researchers at TRM Labs estimated that hackers stole around $2.9 billion in digital assets across nearly 150 attacks last year.
Article Summary: Binance resumes withdrawals of Bitcoin, Ether and some stablecoins on Sunday. The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange said it had replaced 95 per cent of the stolen assets using its own funds. The FBI on Saturday attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a cyber unit sponsored by the North Korean state.

Article Title: Foreign investors withdraw Rs 34,843 crore from Indian stocks; second straight month of selling spree
Article Text:
Representational image

FPI outflows from Indian equities reach Rs 2.95 lakh crore in 2026

Fed decision, valuations among factors behind late-month buying

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) withdrew Rs 34,843 crore from Indian equities in October, marking the second consecutive month of substantial outflows amid concerns over high crude oil prices, global interest rates and the outlook for corporate earnings.However, foreign investors turned net buyers towards the end of the month, purchasing equities worth around Rs 6,300 crore between October 26 and 30.This followed net withdrawals of nearly Rs 2,700 crore in the week ended October 23, according to data from the Central Depository Services Ltd (CDSL).The latest buying indicates an improvement in near-term investor sentiment, although market experts cautioned that a single week of positive flows does not necessarily signal a sustained reversal.Foreign investors had withdrawn Rs 35,861 crore from Indian equities in September. Before that, they invested Rs 20,200 crore in July and Rs 29,631 crore in August.With October's withdrawals, cumulative FPI outflows from Indian equities in 2026 have reached Rs 2.95 lakh crore.Anand K Rathi, co-founder of MIRA Money, said foreign selling remained significant through October, reflecting concerns over elevated crude prices, global interest rates and corporate earnings prospects.“Higher crude prices pose risks to India's inflation and corporate margins, and attractive yields in the US continue to influence global capital allocation,” he said.Rathi added that the sustainability of the recent improvement in foreign flows would depend on greater clarity over global macroeconomic conditions, crude prices and the earnings outlook. He also pointed to the role of domestic institutional investors in absorbing foreign selling and supporting market stability.FPIs were net buyers in three of the four trading sessions ending October 30 in the cash market, suggesting a possible improvement in their outlook towards Indian equities.VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments, said the US Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates unchanged, attractive valuations in Indian large-cap stocks and signs of sustained domestic economic growth could have contributed to the shift in sentiment.The weakening of the global artificial intelligence trade could also be influencing portfolio allocations, he added.The improvement in foreign investment flows helped the Nifty reclaim the 23,000 mark.Vijayakumar said that while foreign investors continued to sell large-cap financial stocks, they were selectively accumulating pharmaceutical and healthcare shares, along with stocks of certain digital platform companies.Pabitro Mukherjee, deputy vice-president for research at Bajaj Broking, said the reversal in FPI flows was encouraging for market sentiment. However, elevated crude prices and global event-related risks could restrict the momentum.Market participants will closely watch the outcome of the US midterm elections in the coming week, along with movements in Brent crude prices, developments in the US-Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts, and quarterly corporate earnings announcements.These factors are expected to remain important drivers of foreign investment flows and broader market sentiment in the near term.
Article Summary: FPI outflows from Indian equities reach Rs 2.95 lakh crore in 2026. Fed decision, valuations among factors behind late-month buying by FPI investors. The improvement in foreign investment flows helped the Nifty reclaim the 23,000 mark. The latest buying indicates an improvement in near-term investor sentiment.

Article Title: ‘Indian manufacturers should target 20% annual growth, exports must drive expansion’
Article Text:
Narayan Sethuramon, co-chairman of the CII International Council

Q: How prepared is the Indian industry to take advantage of the new FTAs?

Q: Will the costs associated with carbon emissions, the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) and Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) outweigh the benefits of the FTA?

Q: Which products and sectors offer the greatest export potential, particularly for SMEs?

Q: European markets are facing geopolitical uncertainty and economic headwinds. How can Indian exporters ensure the FTA gains traction when it becomes operational?

Q: Apart from CBAM and green regulations, what non-tariff barriers are Indian exporters facing in Europe?

Q: Which European markets should Indian companies prioritise?

Q: The UK FTA has been in place for over three months. Has there been a pickup in trade?

Q: Is there a risk of a sudden surge in imports or circumvention under the UK FTA?

Q: Will the ongoing conflict and disturbances in the Gulf region affect the rollout of the India-EU FTA?

Q: How important is export diversification under the UK and EU FTAs, particularly amid uncertainty over the US market?

India’s free trade agreement (FTA) with the UK, which came into force in July, and the proposed pact with the European Union, expected to be signed next month, offer significant opportunities for domestic manufacturers to expand their global footprint.But industry needs to step up efforts to translate tariff concessions into higher exports. Narayan Sethuramon, co-chairman of the CII International Council, says Indian manufacturers should target 20% annual growth, with exports driving expansion.3He explains how companies can tap opportunities in Europe, deal with sustainability requirements and diversify markets amid global uncertainty. Edited excerpts:A: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) account for a significant share of India's exports, and many have been operating in these markets for years. Industry bodies are now playing a major role in taking the benefits of FTAs to companies across regions and sectors. CII is conducting awareness sessions through its regional and state offices.Take textiles, for instance. Under the India-UK FTA, duties on textiles have fallen from 12% to zero. But companies need to understand which products offer the best opportunities - whether home apparel or technical textiles.We have undertaken research and are holding awareness sessions to help members identify these opportunities.CII’s task force on export competitiveness and supply chain resilience has also launched Market Facilitation Services to handhold members through a seven-step process. It starts with identifying opportunities and analysing which FTA and market would work best for a particular company. We then go down to the six-digit HS code level to identify the specific products that offer potential.Government has also done considerable research, identifying products where India already has a dominant market share, those where its share is below 15%, and products that may face additional certification requirements or non-tariff barriers. Government and industry are working together to help SME exporters. It is early days, but there is a structured effort underway.A: Obviously, these costs will eat into margins. We have to be practical about it. But this is where the overall competitiveness of Indian industry comes into play. Even after accounting for regulatory costs, an Indian company could remain more competitive than a rival from another country.We hope the govt will engage with its European counterparts to seek some additional time, at least for small and medium-sized companies in India. Even without that, Indian industry has its own competitive edge. Margins may be slightly lower than expected, but exporters could still secure additional sales at profitable prices.A: FTAs are one cog in the wheel of India's ambition to raise manufacturing’s share of GDP to 25%. Today, it is about 14%. A manufacturing company that merely retains its existing market share in India would grow at the 7-8% rate of the economy. That is not good enough. I believe Indian manufacturing enterprises should target 20% year-on-year growth, with additional growth coming from export markets.Traditional products such as textiles and leather goods have enormous potential. Marine products, engineered goods and foundries, which employ a large number of people, also offer opportunities globally. There is potential in advanced manufactured products such as precision-engineered goods as well.Defence is a good example. Until a few years ago, India barely exported defence products and was a major importer. Today, defence production has expanded significantly. The private sector accounted for 23% of defence production last year, whereas its share was in the single digits or negligible not too long ago. Air conditioners are another segment where exports have grown considerably.We need to focus on both traditional and advanced manufactured goods, keeping in mind the requirements of job creation and economic growth.A: There are three categories of buyers. The first category comprises those who have traditionally been hesitant to source from India, perhaps because of concerns about distance or past quality issues. Indian industry has significantly upgraded the quality of its manufactured products. The FTA also sends a strong signal to European buyers that their govt has entered into an agreement with India and they should consider doing business with us.The second category comprises companies pursuing a China-plus-one strategy. This is no longer limited to the US. European companies are also wary of overdependence on China and are looking at alternative sourcing destinations. We can see more interest in developing additional sourcing options in India.The third category is where Indian companies compete directly by offering better-priced or more competitive products. Here, too, the FTA makes a difference by signalling that India is a trusted partner.However, much more needs to be done through structured buyer-seller meetings. That is where industry and industry associations must step in. We cannot expect govt to do everything. Government has done much of the heavy lifting, and industry must now play its part.A: The issues often relate to certification and testing. Certificates issued by Indian laboratories are not recognised in many European countries. Mutual recognition agreements need to be worked out so that testing conducted in India is accepted. Otherwise, the costs of testing and certification can become prohibitive.Similarly, many European buyers ask for certifications such as EcoVadis. We need more organisations in India that can provide these certifications to Indian suppliers.A: Our first focus should be Germany, Italy, Spain and the Netherlands. Together, these countries represent a huge market for India. India's share of their total imports across many products is in single digits or low double digits, leaving considerable room to grow.For quick wins, we should also focus heavily on the UK FTA. CII's analysis of UK imports shows that India's share is not more than 10% in any of the products analysed. There is tremendous scope for growth.We should be ambitious. Why should the 20% growth target be confined to the services sector? Manufacturing companies should also aim for that rate. For the next five or six years, I would suggest focusing on these markets through a phased approach before expanding to others.A: There has been growth in trade. The target of $100 billion in bilateral trade by 2030 is not unimaginable. It is very much achievable.A: The two economies are quite complementary, and I don’t see a threat of import surges given their relative cost positions. We must recognise that this is different from the first round of FTAs we signed, which were essentially with countries that competed with us.A: They may not affect the rollout, but could influence the pace of growth. India, the US and countries across the world are grappling with higher inflation and uncertainty. India, touchwood, is in a better position than many others, with growth of 7-7.5%.Industry hopes some of these issues will settle down early next year and the world will become more stable. When regions are at war, the willingness to invest is obviously affected. Industry does not like uncertainty.A: We have to look at this in perspective. There have been several positive statements over the last few days on the US trade agreement. We have never looked at the Europe and UK FTAs as replacements for existing sales. They are about diversification and growth.The US has been India's largest merchandise export market for many years and will probably remain so for the next few years. Despite the tariffs, many sectors say their sales have not been affected. Either the US buyer has absorbed the tariff or shared it with the Indian supplier.Export numbers have not declined; in fact, they have increased. Volumes have also remained largely unaffected across many manufacturing sectors.This shows that US customers have been able to pass on price increases to their own buyers, which is ultimately beginning to reflect in US inflation. I don't believe US inflation is driven only by diesel prices or other such factors.From a risk-mitigation perspective, diversifying markets is a sound strategy. However, I personally don’t think sales to the US will decline for most Indian exporters.
Article Summary: Narayan Sethuramon, co-chairman of the CII International Council, says Indian manufacturers should target 20% annual growth, with exports driving expansion. He explains how companies can tap opportunities in Europe, deal with sustainability requirements and diversify markets amid global uncertainty.

Article Title: Commercial LPG cylinder price hiked by Rs 10 to Rs 2,820; ATF rates up for fourth straight month
Article Text:
Commercial LPG rates have been hiked for 2nd straight month

NEW DELHI: The price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder was increased by Rs 10 to Rs 2,820 from Sunday, marking the second consecutive monthly hike. Aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices were also raised by Rs 1.37 per litre, according to state-owned oil companies.Commercial LPG, used mainly by hotels, restaurants and other businesses, had become costlier by Rs 62.50 per cylinder on October 1. The latest increase follows two consecutive monthly reductions of Rs 192 in August and Rs 183.50 in July. Prices had surged to a record high in June amid disruptions to global energy supplies and elevated international rates.A 19-kg commercial cylinder had cost Rs 1,740.50 in February before climbing to Rs 3,113.50 in June. The subsequent cuts brought some relief, but the September and October increases, followed by Sunday's revision, have reversed part of that decline.Meanwhile, the price of a 5-kg Free Trade LPG (FTL) cylinder for a new connection stands at Rs 1,903, while a refill costs Rs 782. FTL cylinders are smaller LPG cylinders sold at market-linked prices, outside the regular subsidised domestic LPG supply system.ATF, the fuel used by aircraft, was raised to Rs 138.50 per litre from Rs 137.12.This is the fourth consecutive monthly increase, following hikes of Rs 5 per litre in August, Rs 6.28 in September and Rs 16 in October. ATF accounts for up to 40 per cent of an airline's operating costs, and the latest increase is likely to add to carriers' expenses.The latest revisions reflect movements in international benchmark prices and the rupee-dollar exchange rate. ATF and commercial LPG rates are revised on the first day of every month and vary across states due to local taxes.Prices of domestic LPG, used by households, remained unchanged at Rs 942 for a 14.2-kg cylinder. Petrol and diesel prices were also left unchanged.
Article Summary: The price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder was increased by Rs 10 to Rs 2,820 from Sunday. Aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices were also raised by Rs 1.37 per litre. Prices had surged to a record high in June amid disruptions to global energy supplies.

Article Title: UPI crosses 25-billion transactions for first time in Oct despite MDR debate; daily value tops Rs 1 lakh crore
Article Text:
In October, UPI transactions soared beyond 25 billion, showcasing remarkable growth in digital payments.

MUMBAI: UPI transactions crossed the 25-billion mark for the first time in October, while average daily transaction value breached Rs 1 lakh crore for the first time, signalling continued growth in digital payments despite the debate over the introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) charges.UPI processed 25.47 billion transactions worth Rs 31.53 lakh crore in October, compared with 24.07 billion transactions valued at Rs 29.37 lakh crore in September. Transaction volumes rose 5.8% month on month, while the value of payments increased 7.4%.The increase was also reflected in daily averages. Average daily transactions rose 2.5% to 822 million in October from 802 million in September, while average daily transaction value increased 3.9% to Rs 1,01,707 crore from Rs 97,913 crore. On a year-on-year basis, transaction volumes grew 23% in October, matching September's growth rate. However, value growth moderated to 16% from 18% in September."The festive season drove this rise. Navratri and the big online sales fell in October, and people used UPI for bigger festive purchases along with their everyday payments. From April to August, the number of UPI payments kept rising, but their daily value stayed flat and the average payment kept getting smaller.In September and October, the value of payments grew faster than their number, and the average payment size went up for two months in a row," said Reeju Datta, cofounder Cashfree. "Last year, Dhanteras and Diwali fell in October, so most of the big festive buying happened in that month. This year, both fall in November. This is the main reason the value of payments grew 16% over last October, slower than the 23% rise in the number of payments. We expect strong growth in November, as the biggest shopping days of the season are still ahead. After the festive season, the important thing to watch will be whether people keep using UPI for larger payments," he added.The October numbers come amid a debate over the introduction of MDR charges, with merchant bodies and sections of the payments industry raising concerns about the potential impact on merchant acceptance and the cost of digital payments. The latest figures, however, show no immediate slowdown in aggregate UPI activity.The increase in October also coincides with the festive season, when spending on shopping, travel and other retail categories typically rises. The monthly figures do not, by themselves, establish the impact of MDR on individual merchant categories.UPI's continued expansion underlines its growing role in retail payments. The challenge for the payments ecosystem will be to sustain this growth while developing a viable revenue model for banks, payment service providers and technology companies that support the infrastructure.
Article Summary: UPI processed 25.47 billion transactions worth Rs 31.53 lakh crore in October. Transaction volumes rose 5.8% month on month, while the value of payments increased 7.4%. Average daily transaction value increased 3.9% to Rs 1,01,707 crore from Rs 97,913 crore.

In a recent conversation with, Impact Catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka unveiled YASHAYuva, Anna, Shiksha, Hunar and Abundance, shaped by nearly 30 years of engagement in national development.The, under the overarching theme of Viksit Bharat 2047, now takes that conversation further. Across five interviews, Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India, explores the experiences, convictions and ideas behind each pillar of the YASHA framework.We begin withAs we approach a world in which machines may become more intelligent than human beings, what is the greatest danger facing our children?The danger is not that machines will become more intelligent. It is that humans may stop thinking and become like robots: programmed to respond, but forgetting how to feel, empathise and connect.Can you share an example of an educational intervention that reflects this philosophy?In the tribal district of Bastar, Chhattisgarh, we taught childrento think, rather thanto think. That was in the 1990s. The greatest moment is not when a child says, "I know the answer." It is when the child asks, "But why?" Today, 30 years later, I feel blessed to be associated with the AM/NS India Times Critical Thinking Championship, which reaches 1 million children each year across 28 states and 8 Union Territories in 14 languages. The scale has changed enormously, but the underlying conviction remains the same.If AI can become a personal tutor to every child, will we still need teachers?More than ever! AI may explain Einstein’s and Newton's laws, but can it recognise the child who has stopped believing in herself? A machine can deliver a lesson, but a great teacher can change a life. AI should be our children's co-pilot, not their autopilot.Are we sometimes confusing marks with intelligence?(Laughs) We give children marks for answering questions correctly. Perhaps we should reward them much more for asking questions nobody else thought of! And who says 100% is the ceiling? Let me tell you a fascinating story. In December 2018, an IIT alum and IAS officer, Ankur Garg, studying at Harvard Kennedy School, scored 171 marks out of 170 in a macroeconomics examination conducted by the world-renowned economist Professor Jeffrey Frankel. Yes, you heard that correctly. 171 out of 170! Now, isn't that wonderful?For me, that is a beautiful metaphor for education and life. Never allow someone else's definition of the maximum to become the limit of your potential. And why restrict this philosophy to examinations? Whether it is knowledge, kindness, compassion or service, give more than is expected of you. After all, a100% cent may be the examiner's limit. It need not be the limit of human potential.Socrates famously argued that the unexamined life is not worth living. Are we losing sight of that larger purpose of education?Absolutely, Socrates was reminding us that a meaningful life must be examined, not merely lived. For him, the pursuit of wisdom was inseparable from virtue. Compassion, honesty, courage, self-discipline and consciousness are not optional extras in education. They are at its very heart.And education is not confined to degrees. Think of the extraordinary wisdom ancient Bharat produced: the, and. Consider Gautam Buddha's teachings on compassion and mindfulness; Lord Mahavira's Anekantavada, which reminds us that truth has many facets and no single viewpoint captures its entirety; Kabir's fearless questioning of dogma; Guru Nanak's message of equality and service; Tulsidas's, with its timeless reflections on duty and devotion, and Kahlil Gibran's timeless wisdom on love, self-discovery and nurturing of independent minds across centuries and civilisations, these extraordinary minds explored not merely how much we can know, but how wisely we can live. Their insights continue to inspire humanity even today. I believe we must cultivate the awareness to discover the possibilities present in the Universe; otherwise, surrounded by information and technology, we risk becoming intellectual zombies!You come from a family blessed with Lakshmi (prosperity), yet your affection for Saraswati (knowledge) seems just as profound!: (With a twinkle in her eyes) I come from a family of geniuses and wizards! My elder brother has one of the world's largest collections of handwritten books/manuscripts. Imagine the centuries of knowledge, imagination and wisdom preserved in those pages. I have never seenandas rivals but as two complementary forces within us.symbolises the subconscious mind, where dreams are born, whilerepresents the conscious mind, which gives direction to the dreams. And remember,does not stay whereis neglected. Wealth without wisdom never creates lasting abundance.We sometimes celebrate the. But listening to you, I wonder whether ais the greater inheritance.(Laughs) Interestingly, I have seen the Silva Mind technique being used by my elder brother for decades – I saw him reading a book about it when he was just fourteen! The power of visualisation fascinated me. I believe it helped him envision extraordinary possibilities and turn them into reality, including the remarkable library he eventually built. But I like your comparison. A silver spoon may feed the body, but a silver mind feeds curiosity. And I must say, there is something wonderful about knowledge. It is perhaps the only inheritance that becomes richer the more you give it away.Which are some of your favourite books?Oh, Sanjiv, that's like asking a mother to choose her favourite child! (Laughs) But a few have stayed with me.opens our minds to spirituality, consciousness and life's infinite possibilities. Then there is Thoreau's, which reminds us that a rich life need not be a complicated one. And I love Ralph Waldo Emerson's essay, with its powerful message about trusting one's own judgment rather than blindly following the crowd. Another favourite isby Richard Paul. And here's a lovely coincidence! Only recently, I discovered that my younger brother has been reading it since the early 1990s! Imagine - all these years, we have been travelling along similar intellectual paths without even realising it.Aruna ji, your closing thoughts?Literacy teaches us to read, education teaches us to understand, and wisdom teaches us to question. Literacy opens the book. Education opens the mind. Wisdom opens the heart. And above all, dream big! But why confine your dreams to the night? Dream during the day, with your eyes wide open, and work to turn those dreams into reality. Imagine 1.4 billion people, each with a dream for Bharat, and each determined to make it happen! When 1.4 billion dreams become 1.4 billion actions, Viksit Bharat 2047 will not be just a vision. It will be our reality!
Article Summary: In a recent conversation with, Impact Catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka unveiled YASHAYuva, Anna, Shiksha, Hunar and Abundance. Under the overarching theme of Viksit Bharat 2047, now takes that conversation further. Across five interviews, Sanjiv Kaura explores the experiences, convictions and ideas behind each pillar of the YASHA framework.

Article Title: Windfall gains tax on diesel, ATF exports up; petrol cut to nil
Article Text:
Centre raises export duties on diesel and ATF, while scrapping the levy on petrol exports for the next fortnight

NEW DELHI: Govt Saturday increased the windfall gains tax on exports of diesel and jet fuel (ATF), while slashing the levy to zero on petrol for the fortnight beginning Oct 31.There is no change in excise duty on petrol and diesel for domestic consumption.According to a notification issued by the finance ministry, the rate of special additional excise duty (SAED) on diesel exports has been increased to Rs 11.5 a litre from Rs 8.5 a litre, while it has been marginally raised to Rs 11 per litre from Rs 10.5 a litre on ATF exports. The duty on petrol exports has been slashed to nil from Rs 2.5 per litre for the next fortnight.The windfall tax - comprising SAED and road and infrastructure cess - on exports of petrol, diesel and ATF was introduced on March 27 to ensure domestic availability of petroleum products by discouraging overseas sales amid the West Asia crisis. The rates are determined by the average international prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF prevailing since the last review.
Article Summary: Government raises export duties on diesel and ATF, while scrapping the levy on petrol exports for the next fortnight. There is no change in excise duty on petrol and diesel for domestic consumption. The windfall tax was introduced on March 27 to ensure domestic availability of petroleum products by discouraging overseas sales amid the West Asia crisis.

Article Title: AAIB for better coordination between civil, defence aviation authorities
Article Text:
AAIB seeks stronger coordination between civil aviation and defence authorities after an Air India Express flight and a Navy aircraft nearly collided on Dabolim runway

NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has sought a greater collaboration between civil aviation and defence authorities as a number of airports where commercial flights operate are defence airfields. Submitting its final report in a case at the Navy’s Dabolim Airport in Goa where an Air India Express flight and a Naval aircraft had ended up on the same runway at the same time, the AAIB has sought the establishment of “a formal framework for collaboration between DGCA/AAIB and defence on a priority basis” to ensure exchange of unclassified information and evidence for investigation of an incident or accident.On April 3, 2026, a scheduled flight of AI Express was to take off from Dabolim for Delhi. Due to misunderstanding and miscommunication between the flight deck and ATC, it entered an active runway when a Naval “fighter was rolling” and the incident was a “near miss”. “On seeing the Navy aircraft at lift off, in the opposite direction the pilot-in-command of AI Express 1109 mentioned to the trainee first officer that the fighter did a low pass, as per the cockpit flight recorder recording,” says the report.In its safety recommendations, AAIB has asked the Airports Authority of India (AAI) “to issue a circular to sensitise air traffic controllers for emphasising the use of standard phraseology and to review the use of phrases like ‘expect backtrack’ by ground controllers which can be easily misinterpreted as ‘enter backtrack’. ATCOs must listen carefully to the read-back and correct any factual error or any apparent misunderstanding. ”The investigator has asked a taxiway of Dabolim airport to be “considered as a hotspot due to its proximity with bays of civil apron and increased probability of the risk of potential ground collisions and runway incursions.”The Navy has been advised to “publish installation of stop bars and their usage at Dabolim airport (and it may) consider establishing a standard frequency change over procedure for civil traffic transitioning from the ground frequency to the tower frequency, in order to avoid recurring confusion regarding the appropriate frequency to be used.”The crew of the AI Express flight has been asked to “undergo counselling and pilot-in-command to undergo training on the safety lapses that resulted in the runway incursion due to lack of operational clarity and communication miss outs.” The airline has to issue a circular to “sensitise all crew for the lapses encountered in this occurrence.”
Article Summary: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has sought a greater collaboration between civil aviation and defence authorities. A number of airports where commercial flights operate are defence airfields. AAIB has sought the establishment of “a formal framework for collaboration between DGCA/AAIB and defence on a priority basis”

Article Title: Indigenous bullet train B28 undergoes 'squeeze test'
Article Text:
India’s indigenous B28 bullet train undergoes a key structural safety test at BEML’s Bengaluru facility ahead of planned trial runs in 2027.

NEW DELHI: New Delhi: The country’s first indigenous high-speed train, B28, has undergone the vehicle body shell test, also known as the “squeeze test”, an important safety assessment to determine whether a train’s car body can withstand heavy external forces and pressure without excessive deformation or structural failure in case of a collision or crash.The test was conducted at BEML’s production facility in Bengaluru. The central PSU is manufacturing the first two of indigenous bullet trains, each comprising eight coaches. The trains have been designed for an operating speed of 249 kmph and a testing speed of 275 kmph, as per a BEML tender document.People aware of the development said the squeeze test is crucial as the trains will operate at high speeds and their car bodies must be capable of withstanding heavy forces in the event of a collision or accident.“After the successful completion of this test, the prototype should ideally be ready in less than six months. Since the B28 (Bharat 28) train is not being built on Japanese Shinkansen technology, the development process should not take much time. The squeeze test establishes whether the body retains its shape under pressure and whether the passenger compartment maintains its structural integrity,” an official said.The railways plans to begin trial runs of B28 on the 100-km Surat-Vapi section of the Ahmedabad-Mumbai High Speed Rail corridor by May-June 2027. Commercial operations on this stretch are scheduled to begin in August 2027.While seeking Cabinet approval for the escalated cost of the country’s first bullet train project, the railway ministry had stated that two prototype trains were expected to be ready for trial runs in the first quarter of 2027. It had also said that the entire Gujarat section of the corridor was expected to be completed by December 2027, while the full 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor is targeted for completion by December 2030.
Article Summary: The test was conducted at BEML’s production facility in Bengaluru. The central PSU is manufacturing the first two of indigenous bullet trains. The trains have been designed for an operating speed of 249 kmph and a testing speed of 275 kmph. The railways plans to begin trial runs of B28 on the 100-km Surat-Vapi section of the Ahmedabad-Mumbai High Speed Rail corridor.

Article Title: GST changes from November 1: Easier registration for online sellers, faster refunds and simpler discount rules
Article Text:
Easier registration for small e-commerce sellers, faster refunds

Easier GST registration for small online sellers

GST registration to become simpler

Faster GST refunds with automated approvals

NEW DELHI: Starting November 1, businesses will see several changes in Goods and Services Tax (GST) procedures, with simpler registration, faster refunds and more flexible rules for discounts offered after a sale.The changes, approved at the 57th GST Council meeting on October 8, are aimed at making GST compliance easier, particularly for small businesses and sellers operating through e-commerce platforms.The reforms mainly cover GST registration, returns and refunds, along with the tax treatment of post-supply discounts. The Council's decisions requiring administrative changes will be implemented in phases beginning Sunday, November 1, 2026.Small businesses selling products through e-commerce platforms across multiple states and Union Territories will no longer need to maintain a physical office in every state where their goods are stored.Under the new rules, eligible sellers passing on input tax credit of up to Rs 2.5 lakh per month can use an e-commerce operator's warehouse as their principal place of business (PPoB) for GST registration in states where they do not have a physical presence.However, sellers must have a genuine physical presence in at least one state, where Aadhaar authentication and physical verification will be carried out. For other states, they can obtain GST registration with the consent of the e-commerce platform, without further involvement of a tax officer.The change is expected to benefit around 9.5 lakh small sellers, helping them expand their reach across India without the additional cost of setting up offices in multiple states. It is also expected to create greater tax parity between competing e-commerce business models.Businesses applying for GST registration can also expect a smoother process from November 1.The GST department has standardised the documents and information required for registration, making it easier for applicants to understand what they need to submit.The GST portal will also offer a more user-friendly interface, with clearer navigation, drop-down lists and tooltips to guide applicants through the process.These changes are expected to reduce errors, unnecessary queries and application rejections caused by missing or incorrect information, while speeding up registration approvals.Businesses waiting for GST refunds could receive their money faster under the new system, which reduces the need for manual intervention by tax officers.Refund claims for the full excess balance available in a taxpayer's electronic cash ledger will be sanctioned automatically by the system, without requiring approval from a tax officer.Similarly, for refund claims related to zero-rated supplies and an inverted duty structure, 90% of the claimed amount will be provisionally sanctioned through an automated process.These provisional refunds will be based on the system's identification and assessment of risks, without direct intervention from tax officers.The government is also easing GST rules for post-supply discounts, addressing a longstanding concern among businesses.Under the revised framework, businesses will have greater flexibility to offer discounts after a sale without having to meet the earlier requirements of a pre-existing agreement or linking the discount to specific invoices.However, safeguards related to credit notes and the corresponding reversal of input tax credit will remain in place.The change is expected to benefit businesses that regularly offer volume-based incentives, trade schemes and year-end rebates.
Article Summary: GST reforms mainly cover GST registration, returns and refunds, along with the tax treatment of post-supply discounts. Small businesses selling products through e-commerce platforms across multiple states and Union Territories will no longer need to maintain a physical office in every state.

Article Title: Tata Sons row: ‘Sebi monitoring all developments,’ says chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey

NEW DELHI: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is monitoring governance-related developments at Tata Sons , the holding company of the Tata Group , chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Saturday. He added that the group's listed companies and their promoters must follow Sebi's disclosure and compliance rules, even though Tata Sons itself is not a listed company.His remarks come amid differences over the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman and whether the holding company should be listed.Speaking on the sidelines of the launch of the Bharat Chamber Investors Forum, Pandey said that the regulatory requirements applicable to Tata Sons were different from those governing the group's listed companies."At the holding company level, there are some issues, as that's not really a listed company. Asked whether SEBI was tracking developments within the Tata Group, he said, "Yes... I mean in the sense of, you know, we have to keep monitoring all the developments."Pandey did not cite any particular governance violation or indicate that the regulator was considering any specific action against the group.The Tata Group has 26 publicly listed companies, with a combined market capitalisation of $328 billion as of March 31, 2025, according to its FY25 annual report.An analysis by governance advisory firm InGovern found that seven of these listed companies together hold around 11.92 per cent in Tata Sons.
