Article Title: Swipe, shop, repeat: Online buyers splash out 7.5% more than offline shoppers
Article Text:
Is onling shopping increasing your bills?

Do you feel your bills have gone up since you started using e-commerce apps? Don’t worry, you are not alone!

Digital shopping still has a long way to go

Groceries make the online basket

Clothing takes the lead among online durable purchases

NEW DELHI:A few taps on your phone could mean a bigger shopping bill. Indian households that use online shopping and payment platforms spend 7.5 per cent more every month than those that do not. The gap is even wider when it comes to services and durable goods. However, the shift to online shopping is far from uniform, with digital adoption still closely linked to household income, according to a report by SBI Research.The report found that households using digital platforms spend 23.4 per cent more on services and 24.5 per cent more on durable goods than those that do not.However, not all households have made the move from traditional shopping to online purchases.Less than half of Indian households have embraced online purchases and payments. According to the report, 45.6 per cent of households used online purchase or payment facilities for at least one consumption item, while 54.4 per cent reported no such usage.The income divide is particularly wide. Among households in the bottom 20 per cent consumption quintile, only 25.3 per cent used online platforms. The share rose to 69.5 per cent among the top 20 per cent, leaving a gap of 44.3 percentage points.The findings are based on a fixed-effects log-linear model that accounts for household characteristics and state-district factors.When it comes to digital purchases, consumables and services account for the largest share at 39.68 per cent, followed by durable goods at 23.3 per cent. Food items, meanwhile, make up just 7.10 per cent of online purchases.Within the food category, groceries lead digital adoption at 4.29 per cent. The numbers drop for everyday fresh produce, with online purchases accounting for 1.32 per cent for vegetables and 1 per cent for fresh fruits. Dry fruits account for 0.62 per cent, while eggs, fish and meat make up just 0.59 per cent.SBI Research attributed the limited adoption of online platforms for perishable food items to households' continued preference for traditional retail channels.Many consumers still prefer visiting markets for their daily food purchases.Not all durable goods are equally popular online.Clothing recorded the highest digital adoption at 19.97 per cent, followed by footwear at 12.05 per cent. Online purchases of furniture, medical equipment and recreational goods, however, remained limited.At the same time, services accounted for the largest share of online purchases within the consumables and services category at 37.93 per cent. Fuel and light followed at 15.96 per cent.SBI Research said digital adoption was associated with higher consumption intensity and more diversified household spending. However, the substantial difference in adoption across income groups shows that the shift towards online shopping is yet to reach all sections of the country equally.
Article Summary: Indian households that use online shopping and payment platforms spend 7.5 per cent more every month than those that do not. Less than half of Indian households have embraced online purchases and payments. Online purchases of furniture, medical equipment and recreational goods remained limited.

Article Title: Centre scraps Rs 2.5/litre petrol export duty, hikes diesel levy to Rs 11.5
Article Text:
Centre scraps petrol export levy, raises diesel duty to Rs 11.5 per litre

NEW DELHI: The Centre has scrapped the Rs 2.5 per litre special additional excise duty (SAED) on petrol exports while raising the levy on high-speed diesel from Rs 8.5 to Rs 11.5 per litre and on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) from Rs 10.5 to Rs 11 per litre, according to notifications issued by the Ministry of Finance on Saturday.The revised rates have been notified by the Department of Revenue through separate excise notifications. While the changes to petrol and diesel duties have been covered under the relevant excise notification, Notification No. 56/2026-Central Excise specifically provides for the increase in the levy on ATF exports.All the revised rates took effect on October 31, the date of their publication in the official Gazette.The export duties on petrol, diesel and ATF were first introduced on March 27, 2026, against the backdrop of the West Asia crisis. The Centre had stated that the move was aimed at discouraging exports to ensure that petroleum products remained available in the domestic market.The introduction of the levies came amid rising international energy prices and uncertainty over supplies, which had raised concerns about the availability of petroleum products within the country.Since then, the government has been revising the duties every fortnight. The exercise takes into account the average international prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF during the period following the previous review.The rates have seen multiple changes since the initial announcement, reflecting movements in international prices. Before the latest revision, the duties stood at Rs 2.5 per litre on petrol, Rs 8.5 per litre on high-speed diesel and Rs 10.5 per litre on ATF, following the October 16 review.
Article Summary: The Centre has scrapped the Rs 2.5 per litre special additional excise duty (SAED) on petrol exports. It has raised the levy on high-speed diesel from Rs 8.5 to Rs 11.5. The export duties on petrol, diesel and ATF were first introduced on March 27, 2026.

Article Title: Binance to resume withdrawals after recovering 95% of $6.3 billion crypto theft
Article Text:
Representative image

FBI links crypto heist to North Korean hacking unit

Trump says investigators are still examining North Korea link

Binance promises customers full reimbursement

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has said it will resume withdrawals in phases after securing 95% of the $6.3 billion in digital assets stolen from its platform in what is being described as the world's largest cryptocurrency heist.The first phase of withdrawals will begin between 0600 and 0900 GMT on Sunday and cover bitcoin, ether, BNB, Solana, XRP, dogecoin and several other tokens, Reuters reported.The exchange said the remaining 5% of the stolen assets comprised less liquid tokens that could take longer to source in the required quantities.Binance announced the update in a post on X late on Saturday.The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has attributed the cyberattack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit.The bureau said on Saturday that members of the group had been observed converting the stolen assets into Ethereum.In a statement, the FBI identified TraderTraitor as responsible for the attack and said it expected further attempts to launder the stolen funds using related technology.The bureau also urged cryptocurrency exchanges, blockchain analytics companies and other industry participants to block transactions associated with identified addresses to prevent the stolen money from being moved to conceal its origins.The FBI said its investigation found that the hackers were converting the stolen assets primarily into Ethereum. It expects the group to attempt further conversions through decentralised finance (DeFi) platforms and instant swap services.TraderTraitor has also been linked to a $1.5 billion hack of cryptocurrency exchange Bybit last year.North Korea has for years denied using state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue generation.US President Donald Trump appeared to question whether North Korea's involvement in the Binance attack had been established.Asked about the incident by reporters at a Halloween party at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Saturday night, Trump said, “I'm not concerned. We're learning about it. We don't know if it's North Korea.”He added that investigators could still determine whether Pyongyang was responsible.Crypto expert Ari Redbord was quoted by news agency AP as saying that he expected the hackers to break the stolen assets into smaller amounts and attempt to move them through smaller exchanges to evade detection. The process could continue for months, he said.“It's bank robbery, in this case, at the speed of the Internet,” said Redbord, chief policy officer at blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs.He added that investigators could track the funds in real time to build cases, disrupt laundering attempts and potentially recover the assets.“It's just this cat and mouse game,” he said.The theft took place on Thursday, when $6.3 billion in bitcoin and other digital currencies was stolen from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.The company said on Saturday that it had set aside enough of the same digital currencies to cover 90% of the missing assets and promised that customers would be fully reimbursed.Binance's latest update said it had now secured 95% of the stolen tokens, allowing it to begin restoring withdrawals in phases. The remaining assets are less liquid and may take longer to obtain in the required amounts.The FBI's warning about further laundering attempts comes as the exchange prepares to resume withdrawals for users affected by the incident.
Article Summary: Binance says it has secured 95% of the $6.3 billion in digital assets stolen from its platform in what is being described as the world's largest cryptocurrency heist. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has attributed the cyberattack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit. US President Donald Trump said investigators could still determine whether Pyongyang was responsible.

Article Title: Binance replenishes 90% of stolen crypto, says it will absorb financial losses
Article Text:
Binance has restored 90 percent of the cryptocurrency assets lost due to a recent security breach. The exchange has pledged to handle the financial repercussions internally, ensuring customers are unaffected.

Binance has replenished 90 per cent of the cryptocurrency assets stolen in a massive security breach, with the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange saying that it will absorb the financial impact of the theft rather than pass the losses on to customers.The exchange has also confirmed that 10 major cryptocurrencies are now fully backed and said it remains on track to resume withdrawals on Sunday, November 1.According to Reuters, Binance said on Saturday that the replenishment includes funds from its corporate treasury and a portion of its futures insurance fund. The exchange is also preparing to partially deploy its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) over the next 24 hours as it continues efforts to replace the remaining affected assets.The exchange said it is purchasing the outstanding stolen assets through cryptocurrency market transactions and over-the-counter (OTC) channels.Binance reiterated that customers would not bear the financial consequences of the security breach, stating that the company would absorb the losses itself."Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the exchange said.Binance said its holdings of Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Tether (USDT), BNB, Solana (SOL), USD Coin (USDC), XRP, USD1, Ripple USD (RLUSD) and Zcash (ZEC) are now fully backed at 100 per cent.The announcement is significant as the exchange seeks to assure customers that their cryptocurrency balances remain supported by sufficient assets despite the theft.Binance also announced that it had taken a fresh Proof of Reserves (PoR) snapshot at 00:00 UTC on October 31. The mechanism allows users to assess whether the exchange holds sufficient cryptocurrency reserves to cover customer balances.The latest announcement comes after Binance suffered a massive security breach on October 29, in which hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from the exchange in what analysts described as one of the largest financial thefts on record.Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis linked the attack with high confidence to North Korean state-backed hackers, citing similarities with previous cryptocurrency thefts attributed to Pyongyang. Binance has not independently confirmed the identity of those responsible.Binance's latest announcement marks a significant step in its efforts to restore customer confidence, with the resumption of withdrawals on Sunday emerging as the next major test for the exchange.
Article Summary: Binance has replenished 90 per cent of the cryptocurrency assets stolen in a massive security breach. The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange said it will absorb the financial impact of the theft rather than pass the losses on to customers. The exchange has also confirmed that 10 major cryptocurrencies are now fully backed.

Article Title: ‘Binance will absorb the impact, not users’: Crypto exchange sets aside $6.34 billion to cover hack losses
Article Text:
Binance sets aside $6.34 billion to cover crypto hack losses

$3 billion in stolen assets frozen

Binance finds additional points of breach in investigation

North Korean hacking group linked to $6.3 billion theft

After facing a major crypto theft, Binance has assured users that they won’t lose money over the breach.The exchange is covering the $6.3 billion loss from its own funds, setting aside more than $6.34 billion to make up for the stolen assets. It has already replaced around 80 per cent of the stolen tokens and is working to restore withdrawal services in phases.So far, Binance has bought back $5 billion worth of the stolen cryptocurrencies, including USDC, USDT, Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and BNB. It is now working on getting the remaining tokens back through market and OTC purchases."This means that we have already covered approximately 80% of the impacted amount. We are actively buying the remaining relevant token assets through market and OTC channels," Binance said.In its second update on the recovery process, the company said the compensation would be funded through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and corporate treasury."We want to be clear about our commitment: Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the exchange said in the statement.The breach took place at around 20:05 UTC on October 29, when Binance's hot wallets were compromised, leading to unauthorised withdrawals of approximately $6.3 billion worth of digital assets.Alongside replacing the stolen assets, the exchange said it had managed to freeze approximately $3 billion worth of the stolen funds across blockchain networks. The effort involved coordination with law enforcement agencies, blockchain intelligence firms, asset issuers and industry partners.Binance is targeting the phased restoration of withdrawal services within approximately 34 hours, although the timeline remains subject to the completion of security checks. Deposits and other platform services unaffected by the breach continue to remain operational.The exchange also plans to release an updated Proof of Reserves report by Monday, November 2, enabling users to check the digital assets backing their account balances.Binance's investigation into the incident has also uncovered more details about how the security breach may have occurred. While the initial assessment pointed towards a compromised laptop, subsequent findings indicated that there were additional points of intrusion."Our initial investigation suggested that the incident may involve a compromised laptop, however, our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach," it said.The company said it had found no evidence of wallet private keys being leaked. Further technical findings are expected within approximately 48 hours, subject to verification.Separately, blockchain investigation firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have linked the $6.3 billion theft to a North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor, Reuters reported.Cybersecurity experts cited by Reuters said money generated through North Korean cryptocurrency thefts has helped finance the country's weapons programmes. However, Binance has not publicly identified the perpetrators and maintained that its investigation is ongoing.The exchange said it would release a detailed technical report explaining how the breach took place, along with the additional security measures it plans to introduce to prevent similar incidents.
Article Summary: Binance has set aside more than $6.34 billion to make up for the stolen assets. It has already replaced around 80 per cent of the stolen tokens and is working to restore withdrawal services in phases. The company said the compensation would be funded through its Secure Asset Fund for Users and corporate treasury.

Article Title: Wall Street reels from tech selloff as Nasdaq posts biggest single-day fall since June
Article Text:
In a surprising turn of events, US stocks experienced significant declines as Intel and Amazon reported disappointing earnings, casting doubt on artificial intelligence investments.

US stocks ended Friday's session with significant losses, as concerns over the scale of investments in artificial intelligence (AI) and the time required to generate returns weighed on investor sentiment. Disappointing quarterly performances from Intel and Amazon further fuelled the technology selloff, pushing the Nasdaq composite to its steepest single-day percentage decline since June 5, according to a Reuters report.The Nasdaq plunged 2.86 per cent to settle at 25,437.00, while the S&P 500 shed 1.82 per cent to close at 7,580.07. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also slipped 1.09 per cent, ending the session at 51,770.31.The technology-focused Nasdaq has now retreated 7.8 per cent from its record closing high registered on October 6. The latest wave of selling came after intel and amazon released their quarterly results late on Thursday, prompting investors to reassess the prospects of companies making substantial investments in AI.Intel shares suffered a steep 28.6 per cent decline, while other major chipmakers also witnessed heavy selling.Nvidia dropped 4.2 per cent and AMD lost 10.9 per cent. The broader semiconductor index tumbled 7.2 per cent, taking its monthly decline beyond 15 per cent.Server manufacturers were not spared either, with Dell shares falling 10.8 per cent and HP declining 9.6 per cent."It's fair to say that this week, not just today, has been very much about the future of AI and what that's going to look like, whether there will be a positive return on investment and if so, how quickly," Oliver Pursche, senior vice president at Wealthspire Advisors in New York, told Reuters.Pursche noted that companies delivering results in line with or above elevated market expectations were continuing to perform well, while those missing targets were facing significant selling pressure.The weakness extended beyond individual stocks. The S&P 500's broader technology sector registered its largest monthly percentage decline since March 2025. Meanwhile, the communication services sector recorded its sharpest monthly fall since April 2022.However, the overall corporate earnings picture remained encouraging despite the market downturn. According to LSEG data cited by reuters, 82 per cent of the 299 S&P 500 companies that had announced their third-quarter results had exceeded analysts' consensus estimates. Analysts had projected year-on-year earnings growth of 31.6 per cent for the quarter.Cryptocurrency-linked stocks also came under pressure following reports that hackers had stolen USD 6.3 billion from binance. Shares of coinbase, strategy and robinhood declined between 7.2 per cent and 10.6 per cent.According to the news agency ANI, All three key US stock indices ended the week in the red, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq also posting losses for the month.
Article Summary: Nasdaq plunged 2.86 per cent to settle at 25,437.00, while the S&P 500 shed 1.82 per cent. Disappointing quarterly performances from Intel and Amazon further fuelled the technology selloff. The Nasdaq has now retreated 7.8 per cent from its record closing high registered on October 6.

Article Title: Nasdaq bleeds: Faces $2 trillion wipeout in October
Article Text:
Nasdaq bleeds: Faces $2 trillion wipeout in October

Nasdaq 100 set to lose over $2 trillion in October as rising AI spending fuels investor concerns

More than $2 trillion in market value is set to be wiped from the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 this month, as Big Tech earnings intensified investor scrutiny of whether the billions being poured into artificial intelligence can generate returns quickly enough.The wipeout would amount to slightly more than SpaceX's entire market value. The index has fallen over 5.8% so far in Oct as the AI trade ran into turbulence, with hyperscalers Meta Platforms, Alphabet and Amazon.com raising spending forecasts further as they race to expand AI infrastructure.The prospect of ever-bigger AI outlays has unnerved investors, particularly as rising borrowing costs threaten to make debt-funded investment more expensive and harder to justify.Alphabet suffered its biggest one-day percentage drop on record on Thursday after disappointing results in the core business of search advertising and a massive acceleration in cash burn. Meta's plans for a record $97.5 billion fund raise heightened concerns about shareholder dilution and whether mounting AI spending could force other Big Tech companies to increasingly tap capital markets.On Friday, Intel's stock led the way lower and was flirting with its worst day since 1974 after tumbling 30%.Microsoft and SpaceX broke from the gloom, with results that showed AI spending starting to pay off."It may be that we've overestimated how strong the growth might be, but they're not going negative in aggregate," said John Bilton, global head of strategic research at Multi-Asset Solutions."We have an insatiable and growing demand for data." Microsoft is reportedly planning to raise about $25 billion through its first US investment-grade bond sale in more than nine years. Among other hyperscalers, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet have issued hundreds of billions of dollars in bond sales over the past four years, worrying investors about overreliance on the medium for raising capital. Morgan Stanley forecast capital spending on AI infrastructure overall will surpass a trillion dollars next year. AI companies' growing reliance on debt funding is emerging as a new risk for investors, challenging the view that the companies at the heart of the boom are insulated from macroeconomic pressures.The concern is spreading beyond stocks to credit markets, where investors are starting to price in the possibility that rising financing costs, combined with slower returns on AI spending, could squeeze companies previously viewed as relatively insulated. Revenue across the "Magnificent Seven" has remained strong since ChatGPT's launch in 2022, showcasing insatiable demand and perhaps why investors were initially willing to back the spending, even as the timeline of payoffs remains uncertain.Amazon's cloud computing cash cow, Amazon Web Services, continued to accelerate, while Meta offered better-than-expected revenue growth and an upbeat outlook. Microsoft also forecast strong cloud growth in its latest earnings report.Big Tech has historically spent heavily on infrastructure to build and expand businesses such as cloud computing, online advertising and e-commerce, but the AI boom has pushed capital expenditure to dizzying levels. JP Morgan expects global AI capex to reach $5.5 trillion by 2030, and sees $900 billion being spent in 2026 alone. Reuters
Article Summary: Nasdaq 100 set to lose over $2 trillion in October as rising AI spending fuels investor concerns. The wipeout would amount to slightly more than SpaceX's entire market value. The index has fallen over 5.8% so far in Oct as the AI trade ran into turbulence.

Article Title: Google loses $500bn as China stocks suffer worst rout since 2016: What's happening to global AI?
Article Text:
Companies are increasingly turning to debt markets to finance the build-out

The bill is getting bigger, but where are the returns?

From chipmakers to China, the sell-off spreads

Investors are asking who can afford the AI race

For the past few years, artificial intelligence has been Wall Street's favourite investment story. Pour billions into chips, build data centres, promise a revolution and watch valuations soar. But the mood music is changing. Investors are beginning to ask an increasingly uncomfortable question: When, exactly, will all this spending start paying off?The answer is becoming more important as some of the biggest names in technology face a bruising week. Google's parent Alphabet suffered a record one-day fall, wiping more than $500 billion off its market value. Intel's shares plunged on a weak outlook, Amazon came under pressure over its spending and sales forecasts, while China's blue-chip stocks recorded their steepest monthly decline in more than a decade.From Silicon Valley to Shanghai, the AI trade is running into a reality check. So what's happening?Alphabet became the latest casualty after its third-quarter results disappointed investors. Its shares fell more than 12% on Thursday, their worst single-day percentage decline on record, wiping roughly $500 billion off its market capitalisation. The company's market value dropped from around $3.97 trillion to $3.46 trillion.The concerns went beyond a quarterly earnings miss. Alphabet reported revenue growth of 25% to $127.6 billion, but its advertising business failed to meet expectations. More significantly, executives acknowledged that Google's AI Mode was generating lower advertising monetisation than traditional search queries.Chief business officer Philipp Schindler said the strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetisation being seen. That admission raised a difficult question: Could Google's attempt to reinvent search with AI end up undermining the advertising business that finances much of its empire?The pressure is compounded by spending. Alphabet recorded $51.4 billion in capital expenditure in the third quarter alone and reported a second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow. Microsoft, by comparison, generated $18.6 billion in free cash flow during the quarter despite its AI investments.Amazon has also faced scrutiny. Its shares fell after it offered a cautious sales forecast for the crucial holiday quarter. The company reported negative cash flow of $42 billion, reflecting the scale of its spending. Chief executive Andy Jassy defended the investment, arguing that cloud services, retail and its own chips could unlock enormous future opportunities.Microsoft has fared relatively better. Revenue rose 19% to $92.3 billion, while its cloud business grew 30% to $63 billion. Its results offered investors evidence that enterprise demand for AI remains strong, even as questions persist over where the technology's long-term value will ultimately accrue.Intel shares plunged more than 25% in premarket trading on Friday after the chipmaker forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion-$16 billion, below analysts' expectations of $17.07 billion. Its finance chief also said the company did not expect positive cash flow this year.The warning dragged semiconductor stocks lower, including Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm and Broadcom. Server makers Dell, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Super Micro Computer also fell, showing how the sell-off is spreading across the AI infrastructure supply chain.China's markets have taken an even harder hit. The CSI300 index fell 8.5% in October, its biggest monthly decline since early 2016, while the technology-focused STAR50 has lost around 40% in less than four months, according to Reuters. The correction has erased roughly $480 billion in market value from Chinese AI and semiconductor leaders.Chinese technology stocks had surged on expectations of strong domestic AI demand and Beijing's push for technological self-reliance. But high valuations, concerns over export restrictions and questions about future demand have undermined the rally. Some popular stocks, including robotics and chipmaking companies, have lost around half their value.The correction also highlights how heavily AI has come to dominate China's markets. Goldman Sachs estimates that AI-related stocks account for 42% of market capitalisation and 57% of turnover across mainland-listed and Hong Kong-listed shares.The scale of the investment explains the growing nervousness. Morgan Stanley expects spending on AI infrastructure to exceed $1 trillion next year. JP Morgan estimates global AI capital expenditure could reach $5.5 trillion by 2030, with $900 billion spent in 2026 alone.Companies are increasingly turning to debt markets to finance the build-out. Meta, Amazon and Alphabet have issued substantial amounts of bonds in recent years, while Microsoft is reportedly planning a $25 billion US investment-grade bond sale. Rising borrowing costs could make this strategy more expensive, particularly if AI revenues fail to keep pace.Investors are already reassessing their exposure. US equity funds recorded net outflows of $6.65 billion in the week ended October 28, their first weekly withdrawals in three weeks, according to LSEG Lipper data.
Article Summary: Companies are increasingly turning to debt markets to finance the build-out. Google's parent Alphabet suffered a record one-day fall, wiping more than $500 billion off its market value. Intel's shares plunged on a weak outlook, Amazon came under pressure over its spending and sales forecasts. China's blue-chip stocks recorded their steepest monthly decline in more than a decade.

Microsoft is reportedly planning to raise around $25 billion through its first US investment-grade bond sale in more than nine years.Other major technology companies have also borrowed heavily. Meta, Amazon and Alphabet have issued hundreds of billions of dollars in bonds over the past four years. This has raised concerns about their increasing dependence on debt to fund their investments.Rising borrowing costs could make it more expensive for these companies to raise money, particularly if the returns from AI investments take longer to come through.Morgan Stanley expects overall spending on AI infrastructure to cross $1 trillion next year.The growing dependence of AI companies on borrowed money is emerging as another risk for investors. It is also raising questions about whether companies at the centre of the AI boom can remain protected from wider economic pressures.The concerns are now spreading beyond stock markets to credit markets. Investors are beginning to consider the possibility that higher borrowing costs and slower returns from AI investments could put pressure on companies that were previously seen as relatively insulated from such risks.Despite concerns about the rising cost of AI investments, revenue across the "Magnificent Seven" has remained strong since ChatGPT was launched in 2022.Strong business performance and demand may explain why investors were initially willing to support the companies' rising spending, even though it remains uncertain when these investments will deliver returns.Amazon Web Services, the company's cloud computing business, continued to see faster growth. Meta reported better-than-expected revenue growth and gave an upbeat outlook. Microsoft also forecast strong growth in its cloud business in its latest earnings report.Big Tech companies have traditionally spent heavily on infrastructure to expand their cloud computing, online advertising and e-commerce businesses. However, the AI boom has pushed their spending to much higher levels.J.P. Morgan expects global spending on AI infrastructure to reach $5.5 trillion by 2030, with $900 billion expected to be spent in 2026 alone.The scale of this year's investments is particularly significant. J.P. Morgan analysts noted that the combined AI spending of Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle and Microsoft this year would likely equal the total amount they have spent since ChatGPT's launch in November 2022.
Article Summary: Nasdaq 100 at risk as investors question whether massive AI investments will pay off quickly enough. Nasdaq index has already fallen more than 5.8% in October as concerns over the AI boom have weighed on technology stocks. Meta Platforms, Alphabet and Amazon.com raising spending forecasts further as they expand their AI infrastructure.

Article Title: Hello Kitty's spy drama lands in hot water: What went wrong with Sanrio in China
Article Text:
Why Sanrio landed in hot water in China

What was the Sanrio-VIVANT collaboration?

Why are Japanese companies facing challenges in China?

Hello Kitty maker Sanrio has come under fire in China over its collaboration with Japanese TV drama VIVANT.The partnership involved a range of soft toys, including Hello Kitty and other characters dressed as spies from the show. However, its storyline, which depicts a fictional Chinese intelligence agency capturing and torturing Japanese spies, upset Chinese audiences.Criticism grew on social media over several days, with Chinese state media also speaking out against the collaboration. Sanrio's Chinese subsidiary eventually announced that it was ending the partnership and all related promotional activities.The incident highlights the challenges foreign companies face in China's lucrative market, where brand associations and public statements can trigger strong reactions. French football star Kylian Mbappe recently faced a similar backlash after remarks about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong prompted several Chinese sponsors to cut ties with him.VIVANT is a Japanese television drama produced by broadcaster TBS and also available on Netflix. The show revolves around Japanese spies and a terrorist organisation called Tent.Its latest season, which is currently being aired, features a fictional Chinese intelligence agency capturing and torturing some of the Japanese spies.This storyline became a point of contention among Chinese audiences following Sanrio's merchandise collaboration.Sanrio's Chinese subsidiary apologised for the controversy and said the partnership did not align with the group's corporate philosophy."We deeply apologize for the concern this has caused everyone," Sanrio's Chinese subsidiary said in a statement."Regarding this collaboration, we believe it contains expressions that are inconsistent with the corporate philosophy of the Sanrio Group. We have therefore decided to terminate this collaboration along with all subsequent projects and promotional activities."TBS did not immediately comment on the cancellation.TBS President Masamine Ryuho said at a regular press conference on Wednesday that the drama is "entirely fictional and has no intention of disparaging any specific country", local media reported.The controversy comes amid strained relations between China and Japan.Tensions increased after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said late last year that a hypothetical Chinese attack on democratically ruled Taiwan could trigger a military response from Tokyo.China has since urged its citizens not to travel to Japan and throttled exports of rare earths to the country. These minerals are important for manufacturing products ranging from cars to weapons.Despite the tensions, Japanese companies, including Sanrio, continue to rely on China for sales.Sanrio recorded sales of 9.8 billion yen ($62 million) in China in the first quarter, almost 25% higher than in the same period a year earlier.Several international companies have faced criticism in China over advertisements and comments. In 2018, Dolce & Gabbana cancelled a fashion show in Shanghai after advertisements showed a Chinese woman struggling to eat pizza and spaghetti with chopsticks.In 2021, H&M, Nike and Adidas also faced criticism over comments about labour conditions in Xinjiang. The recent incidents involving Sanrio and Mbappe are further examples of the challenges foreign companies and celebrities face while operating in the Chinese market.
Article Summary: Hello Kitty maker Sanrio has come under fire in China over its collaboration with Japanese TV drama VIVANT. The partnership involved a range of soft toys, including Hello Kitty and other characters dressed as spies from the show. Its storyline, which depicts a fictional Chinese intelligence agency capturing and torturing Japanese spies, upset Chinese audiences. Sanrio's Chinese subsidiary announced that it was ending the partnership.

Article Title: $6.3 billion gone, North Korea 'link': Inside the crypto heist at world's largest exchange Binance
Article Text:
Binance says it will cover all losses from the suspected hack using its SAFU fund and company money

What happened in the Binance hack ?

Hackers from North Korea?

Why are cryptocurrency exchanges vulnerable?

What happens next?

Hackers stole approximately $6.36 billion in cryptocurrency from wallets held at Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what investigators have described as the biggest crypto heist on record. Blockchain analysis firms have attributed the attack to North Korea's elite hacking unit, while Binance has said it will cover all losses and that user funds are safe.The attack involved the movement of funds across 10 blockchains, with most of the cryptocurrency transferred in about 20 minutes, according to US blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs. As cryptocurrency firms raced to trace and recover the stolen assets, about $3 billion had been frozen by Thursday night in the US, CNN reported.Binance CEO Richard Teng has since said the attack was more complex than initially described, adding that the exchange has found no evidence of a wallet private key leak.TRM Labs said an attacker moved approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets across 10 blockchains."An attacker moved approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes," the firm said in a blog post.Binance's initial investigation indicated that the breach involved an engineer's laptop, which allegedly allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.However, Teng subsequently said the attack was not a simple case of an attacker exploiting one employee's access. "The attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single 'one-click' action," Teng said, according to Reuters, adding that it was a more "complicated attack process".Teng also said the investigation had not attributed responsibility to any individual. The exchange has found no evidence so far that a wallet private key was leaked.The exchange also said it had "temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks are completed; revoked the affected address authorization; [and] engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds".Binance said it was working closely with law enforcement to ensure the matter was handled appropriately. Changpeng Zhao, Binance's co-founder and former CEO, also said he expected user funds to be fully covered by the exchange. Zhao, who stepped down as CEO in 2023 but remains its largest shareholder, said on X that the incident appeared to be a hack.TRM Labs attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean hacking unit, saying its assessment was based on intelligence gathered both on and off the blockchain."TRM attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea's elite hacking unit, based on robust on and off-chain intelligence. We make this judgment with high confidence," the firm said, as quoted by Reuters.Other blockchain intelligence firms have also pointed to North Korea. Singapore-based Pangolin Intelligence said its assessment followed an analysis of transactions associated with the hack and comparisons with previous incidents involving the North Korean cyber unit."Analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents [involving the North Korean cyber unit]" led to the attribution, an analyst with Pangolin Intelligence told CNN.Chainalysis, another cryptocurrency-tracing firm, said it was monitoring the stolen funds as they moved across multiple blockchains, including Bitcoin and Ethereum. A Chainalysis spokesperson told CNN the firm had "high confidence" North Korea was behind the attack.However, the attribution remains an assessment by private intelligence firms and has not been independently established as a confirmed finding by law enforcement.North Korean hacking groups have repeatedly been accused of stealing cryptocurrency and targeting financial institutions. Current and former US and South Korean officials have described cybercrime as a key source of revenue for the sanctions-hit country.In February 2025, North Korean hackers were blamed for an alleged $1.5 billion theft from Bybit, another major cryptocurrency exchange. That incident had set the previous record for the largest crypto heist.North Korean hackers have stolen billions of dollars from banks and cryptocurrency firms over several years, according to reports from the United Nations and private companies.A 2023 CNN investigation also highlighted efforts by South Korean intelligence officials and private cryptocurrency-tracking experts to seize about $1 million in cryptocurrency stolen by North Koreans from a victim.Unlike platforms for trading stocks, cryptocurrency exchanges often hold digital assets on behalf of their users. This can make them attractive targets for hackers seeking to steal large amounts of cryptocurrency, particularly in an industry where regulatory oversight varies.Binance was co-founded in 2017 by Canadian national Changpeng Zhao and became the world's largest cryptocurrency trading platform within a year of its launch.Zhao stepped down as CEO in 2023 after pleading guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws in the US. He was sentenced to four months in federal prison and was pardoned by President Donald Trump in October 2025.Binance has pledged to cover all losses resulting from the incident using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds."Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and company funds," the exchange said, according to Reuters. Teng reiterated the commitment, saying the company was "covering every loss".In its earlier statement also, Binance said it would "cover all losses" from company funds and its emergency assets fund, adding that "user funds are safe".Meanwhile, Cryptocurrency firms are continuing to trace the stolen funds and attempt to prevent the attackers from converting or moving the assets beyond recovery.A Pangolin Intelligence analyst told CNN that the effort to track the stolen cryptocurrency was still in its early stages. "I think the cat and mouse game has barely begun yet," the analyst said, adding that North Korea was likely poised to tap a network of money-laundering organisations to cash out the stolen funds.The recovery effort will depend on how much of the cryptocurrency can be traced and frozen before it is moved through other wallets or converted into assets that are harder to recover.Bitcoin and Ether, the two most widely traded cryptocurrencies, fell following news of the Binance breach but recovered some losses. They were trading about 2 per cent to 3 per cent lower by midday Friday in Hong Kong.
Article Summary: Binance says it will cover all losses from the suspected hack using its SAFU fund and company money. About $3 billion had been frozen by Thursday night in the US, CNN reported. Binance CEO Richard Teng has since said the attack was more complex than initially described.

Article Title: World's largest crypto exchange Binance probes 'security breach', $6.3 billion in assets impacted
Article Text:
Suspected hack hits world's largest crypto exchange Binance (Reuters photo)

Tether, Circle freeze funds linked to incident

Binance investigates possible access through employee laptop

According to Google Trends, searches for ‘binance hacked’ surged by over 5,000% in India in the past 24 hours.

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, is investigating a potential security breach that could have affected assets worth around $6.3 billion, the company said on Thursday. However, it has not confirmed whether funds were stolen or established the full extent of the damage.Blockchain analysis firm TRM said North Korea was behind the $6 billion crypto hack on Binance.The exchange said it was working to resolve the issue and had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while conducting security checks and coordinating with law enforcement and industry partners.“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” a Binance spokesperson said in a statement, adding that its security teams were reviewing all relevant information and would provide updates through official channels once the details were verified.In a post on X, Binance said its estimated total impact stood at around $6.3 billion, with roughly $3 billion in affected assets frozen on the blockchain so far. The company added that it was working with blockchain partners to trace and freeze additional funds.Binance's initial investigation suggested that the incident may have involved a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allegedly allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.The exchange said it had found no evidence of a wallet private key leak. It added that further technical details would be released after the investigation was completed and the findings fully verified.Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle have also frozen assets associated with the potential breach.Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company had frozen more than $1.5 billion in assets linked to what he described as a potential Binance exchange hack. Circle co-founder and CEO Jeremy Allaire said the company had frozen more than $800 million in associated funds in coordination with law enforcement.Binance said it was working with law enforcement agencies, token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and other industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.Changpeng Zhao, Binance's founder who stepped down as CEO in 2023, also described the incident as a possible hack in a post on X.“User funds are safe!” Zhao wrote, adding that although he no longer managed Binance, he expected all user funds to be fully covered as a shareholder.The incident has also coincided with pressure on cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin fell 3.2% on Thursday evening, slipping below $79,000.The suspected compromise of a DevOps engineer's laptop has emerged as a key line of inquiry. According to Binance's preliminary assessment, the attacker may have used access to a service container to initiate unauthorised withdrawals.The company has not confirmed the identity of the attacker or established whether the incident resulted in a loss of user funds. It said it would release more technical information after verifying the facts.The episode adds to persistent security concerns in the cryptocurrency industry, where exchanges and other platforms remain targets for cyberattacks and unauthorised transactions.Founded in 2017, Binance allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets and has grown into the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. Zhao stepped down as CEO in 2023 after pleading guilty to a felony related to failures to prevent money laundering on the platform. US President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.
Article Summary: Search for ‘binance hacked’ surged by over 5,000% in India in the past 24 hours. Tether, Circle freeze funds linked to incident. Binance investigates possible access through employee laptop. North Korea was behind the $6 billion crypto hack on Binance.

Article Title: 1.14 lakh startups generate more than 12 lakh jobs in India: Finance ministry
Article Text:
Finance Ministry

NEW DELHI: More than 1.14 lakh startups in India have created over 12 lakh jobs so far, the finance ministry said in its latest review of the Indian economy.In the report titled, ‘The Indian Economy: A Review January 2024’, the Department of Economic Affairs said that the 1.14 lakh startups recognised by the government under the 'Startup India initiative’ created more than 12 lakh jobs (as of October 2023).The state-owned e-commerce platform Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) clocked more than 63 lakh transactions till November 2023, the document read.Despite facing global challenges in 2023 like valuation issues, few IPOs, regulatory changes and macroeconomic and geopolitical trends, India remains the third largest tech start-up ecosystem globally, with over 950 tech startups founded last year.The cumulative funding for more than 31,000 tech start ups has exceeded $70 billion (from 2019 to 2023), according to a recent report by Nasscom in collaboration with Zinnov.“In 2023, despite facing global economic and regulatory challenges, Indian tech startups have prioritised the imperative of enhancing their business fundamentals, driving profitability and growth,” said Debjani Ghosh, President, Nasscom.“The proliferation of tech startups in tier 2 and 3 cities marks the ecosystem's resilience,” she added.Navigating 2024, tech startup founders expect to continue the revenue growth path with measured steps focusing on optimising expenditure and maximising profitability for B2B tech startups.Investments in deeptech will continue an upward trend in 2024. With generative AI (GenAI) acceleration, 70 per cent of start-up founders are embedding artificial intelligence (AI) in their solutions.As funding becomes scarce for the Indian startup ecosystem in general, the explosion of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has given a new lease of life to entrepreneurs and founders in the country, as the Centre extends support to the sector.
Article Summary: The state-owned e-commerce platform Open Network for Digital Commerce clocked more than 63 lakh transactions till November 2023. India remains the third largest tech start-up ecosystem globally, with over 950 tech startups founded last year. The cumulative funding for more than 31,000 tech start ups has exceeded $70 billion.

Article Title: Startups Revolutionizing Carbon Dioxide into Valuable Products
Article Text: For most perfume makers, ingredients to make it smell great are the most important feature. But for Stafford Sheehan, a cofounder and chemist at Air Company, the most important part of perfume-making has no scent at all.New York-based Air Company uses technology that converts planet-warming carbon dioxide into ethanol, which is then blended with essential oils and water to produce perfume. While the pale yellow-color Air Eau de Parfum is about 50% more expensive than Coco Chanel’s signature No. 5, Sheehan says his product is uniquely valuable: Every 50-milliliter bottle uses 3.6 grams of CO2 that otherwise would have been released into the atmosphere. Its package reads: “Turning CO2 into something beautiful.”While the volume of CO2 utilized in the bottle is extremely small, Air Company’s perfume showcases one way the coming wave of captured carbon can be put to use. Renewable energy and electric cars alone won’t be enough to cut CO2 emissions to zero. The world will almost certainly need to capture billions of tons of the gas annually in the coming decades. Large amounts will likely be stored underground.Using it — so-called carbon capture and utilization, or CCU — to create new products from perfume to jet fuel could be an important tool in the fight against climate change, too, though the nascent industry has major hurdles to overcome.Roughly 230 million tons of CO2 are utilized every year, according to a 2019 report by the International Energy Agency. While roughly one-third of that is reused to force more oil from the ground — hardly a carbon-neutral process — CCU advocates say that the number of companies coming up with new uses for carbon has mushroomed in recent years, paving a way to unlock climate benefits. Carbon-derived fuels and chemicals, for example, could theoretically grow to the scale of billions of tons of CO2 use per year if companies could perfect their technology and lower costs.Calgary-based CleanO2 transforms CO2 captured from building heating boilers into feedstock to make soap. Newlight Technologies, a biotechnology startup based in California, takes carbon pulled directly from the air and turns it into biodegradable plastics. Germany’s Covestro AG, one of the world’s largest polymer manufacturers, is also switching some of its fossil fuel-based feedstocks to carbon-derived materials for everything ranging from car shells to medical devices and stadium roofs.Most companies working on CO2-sequestering products are still in their infancy. To grow the emerging sector, global venture capitalists in 2022 poured nearly $500 million into carbon utilization businesses, according to the IEA. That’s in stark contrast to 2015, when barely any venture money went to technologies that utilize CO2.“It’s just a whole different landscape today than it was a decade ago,” says Sasha Mackler, executive director of the energy program at Washington, DC-based non-profit Bipartisan Policy Center.Jennifer Holmgren, chief executive officer of LanzaTech Global Inc., has experienced the shifting sentiment firsthand. The Illinois-based company uses a carbon-eating bacteria – discovered in the guts of rabbits and preserved as powder – to make alternative ethanol in bioreactors not dissimilar to how breweries ferment beer. In the early 2010s, when Holmgren touted carbon-derived ethanol to prospective customers, her sales pitch was met with skepticism.But the tide began turning later that decade. In 2018, the company’s jet fuel produced from the emissions of a Chinese steel mill helped power a Transatlantic flight. LanzaTech has also inked agreements with airlines including Japan’s All Nippon Airways to supply CO2-derived jet fuel. And LanzaJet, the company’s spin-off, plans to start producing sustainable jet fuels at a commercial scale this year.Yet for all the hype around sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) using captured carbon, the industry is still an extremely small player. Almost every major airline in the world has pledged to use at least 10% sustainable jet fuels by 2030, yet SAF makes up only 0.1% of global aviation fuel supply — and much of it is made from sources other than captured CO2, such as used cooking oil.“There’s a lot more interest because consumers have become much more interested in buying things that are lower carbon,” says Holmgren. That’s enabled LanzaTech to expand the number of products that utilize CO2.American plastic container maker Plastipak, for instance, has partnered with LanzaTech to produce carbon-derived packaging materials, while polyester converted from LanzaTech’s ethanol has replaced its petroleum-based counterpart at a pilot scale in Lululemon shorts, Zara dresses, H&M yoga pants, On running shoes and Craghoppers jackets. Like SAF, though, there’s still a long way to go for CO2-derived polyester to reach meaningful levels of use.Momentum to grow beyond one-off products and low-scale production has also been supercharged by a growing array of regulations and incentives around the world. For instance, the Inflation Reduction Act that US President Joe Biden signed in 2022 raised the tax credit for carbon capture and utilization by more than 70% to $60 per metric ton in an effort to make costly projects more financially appealing.To keep the climate within habitable limits, the IEA estimates that carbon capture will have to grow to 7.6 billion tons of CO2 annually by mid-century. CCU will play a role, though just how big remains to be seen. Not every use case is created equal and some approaches, such as dissolving compressed CO2 in water to make carbonated beverages, only store the gas temporarily. To quantify the true climate benefit of carbon utilization, experts say third-party verification is badly needed.The rise of CCU technology comes as another key approach in President Biden’s net-zero roadmap is hitting a bit of a wall. Carbon capture and storage — that is, gathering CO2 as it’s released from a coal-fired power plant or other emissions source and sequestering it underground — has faced challenges because carbon is often captured in one place and stored in another. That requires pipelines to transport the gas, which many local communities have opposed. Blackrock-backed Navigator, for example, recently announced it was scrapping a planned 1,300-mile CO2 pipeline.Carbon utilization companies say that they can sidestep that issue by using carbon near or at where it’s captured.At its 12-acre factory in Brooklyn, Glenwood Mason Supply demonstrates how. The concrete manufacturer takes CO2 captured at a residential building by its partner company, CarbonQuest, and uses a technique licensed from low-carbon concrete startup CarbonCure to convert the compressed carbon into a powder not unlike dry ice. It then injects it into industrial mixers. There, the CO2 meets cement, sand and aggregate, setting off a series of chemical reactions. The final result is concrete blocks with CO2 sealed in.The technique not only stores carbon but it can also make the blocks marginally stronger. The company estimates that it has utilized about 100 tons of CO2 in total since 2020. Even if the blocks break down, the stored carbon won’t be released as CO2 because it’s been mineralized.“Cement is a big offender in carbon emissions,” says Constance Cincotta, founder of the concrete factory. She became intrigued by the technology and its ability to lower her company's climate impact after hearing about it at an industry conference in the early 2010s. But it wasn't until CarbonCure came on the scene a few years ago that the prospect of CO2-storing cement became tangible. Glenwood Mason then sourced CO2 locally from CarbonQuest, which captures carbon from buildings in New York. Those factors have enabled large-scale production.While Cincotta’s intended to help the planet, she and her team discovered that sinking CO2 into concrete blocks is good for the business, too. In 2019, New York City — where the majority of the company’s concrete blocks are sold — passed a regulation requiring all buildings to shrink their carbon footprint 40% by the end of the decade. Glenwood Mason’s phones have been ringing ever since, with calls from architects and property developers who want to leverage their lower-carbon building materials to cut emissions, says Jeff Hansen, the company’s vice president in architectural sales and marketing.The factory’s CO2-storing concrete blocks also caught the eye of Amazon.com Inc, which in 2022 persuaded a real estate developer to purchase roughly 50,000 blocks for the construction of a new warehouse in New York that Amazon has leased. Had Glenwood Mason not sealed CO2 in its blocks, it wouldn’t have won the contract, Hansen says. To figure out how to pack more carbon into its products, the company has set up a laboratory in its factory to test the reaction between CO2 and other concrete feedstocks under different temperatures and humidity levels.But figuring out the right formula is only one consideration. Utilizing CO2 often comes with an additional cost. As the demand for CO2-derived products climbs, that green premium is expected to go down. Yet “it’s very hard to be a cost parity with a 100-year-old industry that doesn’t even have to pay for its externalities,” says Holmgren of LanzaTech. Even with economies of scale, Holmgren estimates that carbon-containing fabrics will still likely cost as much as 20% higher than conventional ones.“It’s unlikely that we will ever be a cost parity,” she says.In addition to the cost barrier, CCU companies also have to convince end users that may be suspicious of unproven new technologies.Changing feedstocks “does come with risks,” says Keith Wiggins, chief executive officer of Econic Technologies, a British startup that specializes in making carbon-derived chemicals. To get risk-averse industries onboard, Wiggins says his company is laser-focused on those that are under consumer pressure to change course.That strategy seems to be working. Econic has teamed up with three manufacturers in the US, China and India to produce mattresses, outdoor garments and building insulation materials that utilize CO2. The first batch of products using the company’s technology are scheduled to enter the market in 2024.For all the promise of the carbon utilization industry, it remains to be seen if it can challenge the status quo. While Air Company started selling carbon-derived perfume in 2021, the startup has yet to build its first commercial plant, Sheehan says, citing the time-consuming process needed for collecting data and fine-tuning the technology for large-scale production.Fow now, the company’s demonstration facility in New York City — where CO2 and hydrogen gas flow through tubes into a reactor to form chemical reactions, aided by catalysts made from a confidential mixture of metals — is designed to yield at least 10,000 gallons of CO2-derived liquid annually. The limited production capacity has left many orders for its perfume — as well as jet fuels and Air Vodka, another popular product made from CO2 — unfilled.“We need to scale these facilities to the size of oil refineries today in order to have the impact on climate change that we want to have,” Sheehan says.
Article Summary: New York-based Air Company uses technology that converts planet-warming carbon dioxide into ethanol, which is then blended with essential oils and water to produce perfume. Carbon-derived fuels and chemicals, for example, could theoretically grow to the scale of billions of tons of CO2 use per year if companies could perfect their technology.

Article Title: E-commerce firm Udaan raises $340 million ahead of planned IPO
Article Text: Indian e-commerce firm Udaan raised $340 million to strengthen its supply chain and boost vendor partnerships ahead of a stock market debut planned for 2025.The Series E round was done via a combination of fresh equity and conversion of debt, the Bangalore-based company said in a statement Thursday. The round was led by M&G Plc and existing investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners and DST Global participated.The round “fully funds our business plan,” Vaibhav Gupta, Udaan co-founder and chief executive officer, said in the statement. “It enables our continued journey of growth and profitability, positioning us well to be public-market ready in the next 12-18 months.”Udaan, which competes with Reliance Industries Ltd. and Walmart Inc.’s Flipkart in helping smaller merchants source their goods, runs an online marketplace and logistics networks that help mum-and-pop stores get quicker deliveries and cut traditional middlemen out. That kind of digital-led wholesale business, though a very small part of India’s overall retail market, is expected to swell to $150 billion in sales in a decade, according to McKinsey & Co.The startup targets an initial public offering in 2025, though it’s yet to decide whether it will do so in India or overseas, Gupta told Bloomberg News last month.Udaan was founded in 2016 by three engineers who previously worked at Flipkart. The trio together ran the company until Gupta, one of the founders, took over as CEO in 2021. The other two founders — Amod Malviya and Sujeet Kumar — are board members.
Article Summary: Indian e-commerce firm Udaan raised $340 million to strengthen its supply chain. The Series E round was done via a combination of fresh equity and conversion of debt. The startup targets an initial public offering in 2025, though it’s yet to decide whether it will do so in India or overseas.

Article Title: Minuscule AI startup raises $41 million to tap India growth
Article Text: A generative artificial intelligence startup targeting the Indian market raised $41 million in fresh funding, the largest such round by an early-stage AI contender in the country.Sarvam AI is building large language models targeted at unique uses in Indian languages at price points that the country’s 1.4 billion people can afford. The Series A funding round was led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, and participants included Silicon Valley billionaire Vinod Khosla’s Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners, formerly Sequoia Capital India & Southeast Asia, Sarvam said Thursday.The Bangalore-based startup, until recently in stealth mode, was co-founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar. It has ambitious plans to build open source foundational AI systems as well as tools for creating apps for the meager compute infrastructure available to developers in India. The startup has a total of 18 employees and is just opening an office in the city."What we are showing is that you can build large language models with limited resources,” Raghavan said in a phone interview. "We are building at a smaller scale and demonstrating that these can be extremely cost and energy efficient so they can be accessed by everyone."Large language models, like OpenAI’s GPT-4 and Meta Platforms Inc.’s Llama, are powerful AI systems that understand by learning from vast amounts of diverse data from the internet and elsewhere to summarize, translate, and create text, audio and video for a wide range of applications. The rivalry to develop ever-more sophisticated models is heating up in Silicon Valley and such efforts have attracted billions of dollars in investments.
Article Summary: Sarvam AI is building large language models targeted at unique uses in Indian languages. The Bangalore-based startup, until recently in stealth mode, was co- founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar. It has ambitious plans to build open source foundational AI systems.

Article Title: ZestMoney set to shut operations this month
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Buy now Pay Later (BNPL) startup ZestMoney has decided to shut operations. The move will impact some 150 employees of the firm, the company's management told employees in a town hall on Tuesday. ZestMoney did not comment. It is learnt that the firm will shut down by the end of this month.The move comes after attempts by the Bengaluru-based startup to get acquired by larger peer PhonePe failed. The deal was called off earlier this year after a due diligence process undertaken by PhonePe, while evaluating the potential acquisition failed to meet its bar. The Walmart-owned fintech major had, however, hired some 130 of ZestMoney's employees.
Article Summary: The move will impact some 150 employees of the firm, the company's management told employees in a town hall on Tuesday. The move comes after attempts by the Bengaluru-based startup to get acquired by larger peer PhonePe failed. The Walmart-owned fintech major had, however, hired some 130 of ZestMoney's employees.

Article Title: Startups will play important role in helping India become 3rd largest economy: CEA Nageswaran
Article Text:
Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran





THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Startups will play an important role in helping India become the third largest economy in the world, Chief Economic Advisor (CEA) to the Union government V Anantha Nageswaran has said.Nageswaran said that tier-2 and 3 cities, including Kerala's capital, have become game-changers in helping startups flourish in the country due to improvements in infrastructure and supportive policies of the government, according to a KSUM release.The CEA, during his Leadership Talk on the concluding day of the Huddle Global 2023 organised by the Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), said that India was the fifth largest economy on course to become the third largest in a few years."In fact, I will say 7-in-7 is the buzz slogan, that is 7 trillion USD economy in seven years. Seven trillion USD economy size by 2030 is possible if India maintains its present growth trajectory, and in that journey startup entrepreneurs are going to play an important role," he is quoted as having said in the release.He was of the view that the active participation of startups in India in developing business models on the foundation of expanding physical and digital infrastructure will continue to generate efficiency, revenue and economic returns for the country."The last decade has seen an exceptional transformation in the startup landscape in India, which has emerged as the third largest ecosystem globally, with over 1.12 lakh startups presently recognised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) across 763 districts."Among them, more than 110 are unicorns with a total valuation of around USD 350 billion," he said.The CEA further said that the country ranks second in innovation quality.He said that innovation in India was not just limited to certain sectors as startups were solving problems in 56 industrial sectors, with 13 per cent of them from IT services, nine per cent from health and life sciences, seven per cent from education, five per cent from agriculture and five per cent from food and beverages.Nageswaran also said it was significant that 49 per cent of the startups were from tier-2 and 3 cities which have turned to be game-changers as the business advantages in these locations enable entrepreneurs to operate at lower costs as compared to tier-1 cities."Apart from improved infrastructure and the government's pro-active policies, the availability of a technically skilled talent pool is a huge advantage for startups to set up and flourish in tier-2 and tier-3 cities," he said.He said that historically there was a perception that small towns were difficult places to conduct business."...but with improved internet penetration, vastly better physical infrastructure, road, rail and air connectivity and supportive government policies, this is no longer true," he said.He also noted Kerala's startup journey has been an inspiring one.The CEA said that KSUM has served as the catalyst since its establishment in 2006 to promote change that propelled the state into the forefront of the global startup arena.KSUM is the Kerala government's nodal agency established in 2006 for entrepreneurship development and incubation activities in the state.Nageswaran said that with over 4,000 registered tech startups, 63 incubators and 10 lakh square feet of incubation space, KSUM has not only met its goal of promoting technology-based entrepreneurship but has also earned the distinguished position of being among the world's top business incubators.The November 16-18 fifth edition of Huddle Global, India's biggest beachside startup conclave, was organised by KSUM at Adimalathura beach, near Vizhinjam, here.Attended by around 1,500 delegates, the event displayed sophisticated products from emerging sectors such as robotics, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, life sciences, space tech, blockchain, IoT, e-governance, fintech, healthtech, agritech, edutech and SaaS from across the country.
Article Summary: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran said tier-2 and 3 cities, including Kerala's capital, have become game-changers in helping startups flourish in the country. CEA said that India was the fifth largest economy on course to become the third largest in a few years.

Article Title: E-Commerce startup Udaan to trim costs ahead of 2025 IPO
Article Text: E-commerce startup Udaan is working to curb costs and forge new partnerships with consumer brands in India as it prepares to go public in 2025.Udaan, which competes with Reliance Industries Ltd. and Walmart Inc.’s Flipkart in helping smaller merchants source their goods, will make an operating profit within 18 months, Chief Executive Officer Vaibhav Gupta said in an interview. That’s set to happen around the same time as its initial public offering, he said.The priority “is steady and predictable financial performance,” Gupta said. “Second, strategically we want to ensure that we are top of mind with shopkeepers, with big manufacturers, and we maintain our relative market share.”Lightspeed Venture Partners-backed Udaan is among startups trying to tap the rapid growth of India’s economy and consumer market, while meeting investor demands for profitability. Udaan, which at its peak employed thousands, joined fellow Indian startups in slashing jobs last year and tightening internal controls and compliance. It now has about 1,800 staff, and Gupta didn’t specify if further job cuts are needed.Corporate governance lapses at Indian online tutoring firm Byju’s, once the country’s top startup with a valuation of $22 billion, shone a light at unique challenges faced by founders in the South Asian nation and drove companies to be more diligent.“We continue to move towards more professionalized management, professionalized board and also institutionalized shareholders as we go towards public markets,” Gupta said.Udaan is yet to decide whether it will list in India or overseas. It was valued at more than $3 billion in a 2021 funding round, and was in talks to raise $400 million, Business Standard reported in September. Lightspeed owns about 35% of Udaan, while Tencent Holdings Ltd. holds 6%.The company was founded in 2016 by three engineers who previously worked at Flipkart. The trio together ran Udaan until Gupta, one of the founders, took over as CEO in 2021. The other two founders — Amod Malviya and Sujeet Kumar — are board members.Udaan built an online marketplace and logistics networks that help mum-and-pop stores get quicker deliveries and cut traditional middlemen out. That kind of digital-led wholesale business still accounts for a very small part of India’s overall retail market but can balloon to $150 billion in sales and yield a 100% return on capital invested in a decade, according to McKinsey & Co. estimates published in the Mint newspaper.Bengaluru-based Udaan has also ventured into financing through its fintech unit which helps shopkeepers get working capital loans to buy inventory. That business is profitable before taxes and is growing 70% annually, Gupta said.“That’s a second business in the overall umbrella of Udaan trying to organize trade in the country,” Gupta said. “In addition to commerce, financing becomes an important market opportunity.”
Article Summary: Udaan will make an operating profit within 18 months, Chief Executive Officer Vaibhav Gupta says. Udaan competes with Reliance Industries Ltd. and Walmart Inc.’s Flipkart in helping smaller merchants source their goods. The priority “is steady and predictable financial performance,” Gupta said.

Article Title: Kerala-based startup bags prestigious awards
Article Text: KOCHI: A company under the Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), which primarily connects devotees with temples through a cost-free Customer Relationship Management Solution (CRM), has bagged two prestigious awards in a week's time, boosting its profile fuelled by three years of ground-breaking ‘BookSeva'.InIT Solutions Pvt Ltd was honoured with the ‘ Emerging Startup of the Year 2023 Award ', followed by another at the Entrepreneurship Conclave 2023 (EC2023) earlier this month, a press release said here on Saturday.The 2011-founded InIT, whose CRM solution is tailored specifically for temple administration, won the first of the two honours on September 30 at the HSX2.0 event hosted by Headstart at SAP Labs Bangalore, it said.The second came at the October 7-8 EC2023 organised by the World Konkani Centre, Saraswath Chamber and UK & Co, it said.InIT won the ‘Emerging Startup' recognition at a competition between 1,000 startups from across the country.The company emerged in the standout selections among the 70 startups shortlisted, earning it the spotlight at the Bharath Pitchathon 2.0, it said.As for the EC2023 honour, the event recognised InIT Solutions Pvt Ltd as one of the ‘Top 5 Startups' that had excelled in the SharkTank Pitching competition.The event was held before experts such as Infosys former director Mohandas Pai and Jyothi Labs ex-CEO Ullas Kamath besides 300-plus visionary entrepreneurs, investors and corporate representatives from across India.Each of these top startups, including InIT, won a prize of Rs 5 lakh, the statement further said.Besides ‘BookSeva', InIT assists temples in streamlining their day-to-day operations by implementing an ERP (enterprise resource planning) system.Notable Kerala temple administrations associating with InIT are Guruvayur, those under Cochin Devaswom Board and Attukal in Thiruvananthapuram district.InIT Solutions, which is based at Vennala in the city, is working towards expanding its services to temple management across India, it added.KSUM is Kerala government's nodal agency established in 2006 for entrepreneurship development and incubation activities.
Article Summary: InIT Solutions Pvt Ltd was honoured with the ‘ Emerging Startup of the Year 2023 Award' The company primarily connects devotees with temples through a cost-free Customer Relationship Management Solution (CRM) The 2011-founded InIT, whose CRM solution is tailored specifically for temple administration, won the first of the two honours.

Article Title: Startup BharatAgri raises Rs 35 crore from investors
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Agritech startup BharatAgri, an advisory led e-commerce platform for farmers, on Thursday said it has raised Rs 35 crore (USD 4.3 million) from investors including Arkam Ventures.The company raised Rs 35 crore in the Series A funding round.Besides Arkam Ventures the funding round also saw participation from Capria Ventures and existing investors, India Quotient, 021 Capital , and Omnivore , BharatAgri said in a release.The funding marks Arkam Ventures' third investment in the agri-tech space."The funds will be used to scale BharatAgri's e-commerce platform into new geographies and strengthen its last-mile delivery," the statement said.BharatAgri, founded by IIT Madras Alumni Siddharth Dialani and Sai Gole, has built prediction algorithms that provide advisory customised to crops, region and climatic changes.Farmers can access this custom advisory that would help them increase farm yield, lower input costs and labour effort.Its e-commerce platform offers over 10,000 agricultural products such as fertilisers, seeds, pesticides, insecticides, farming equipment, among others and is delivered pan-India, the statement said.
Article Summary: Agritech startup BharatAgri, an advisory led e-commerce platform for farmers, on Thursday said it has raised Rs 35 crore (USD 4.3 million) from investors including Arkam Ventures. The company raised Rs35 crore in the Series A funding round. The funding round also saw participation from Capria Ventures and existing investors, India Quotient, 021 Capital, and Omnivore.
